programme.title: Duncan Mackenzie - Dileab a' Ghlinne
programme.desc:
’S e stàcair agus eòlaiche eachdraidh-ionadail a th’ ann an Donnchadh MacCoinnich – fear a tha dìoghrasach mu bhith a’ toirt am bàrr eachdraidh a shinnsearan ann an Gleann Inbhir Làthail.
A' leantainn air fiolm shoirbheachail ann an 2022, bidh sinn air sàilean Dhonnchaidh agus an rannsachadh aige a’ gabhail ceum mòr. Air an ùr-lorg, tha clàran sgrìobhte a’ dol air ais gu 1370 a’ toirt sealladh prìseil de bheatha dhùthchail Alba, is tha meud na coimhearsnachd seo – fichead mìle ceàrnagach– a’ daingneachadh a cudromachd.
’S e an t-eòlas gun choimeas a tha aig Donnchadh mu na cnuic is na glinn a tha air ar stiùireadh gu mòr-adhartas is chun na luirg smuaineachail gun fhaoidte gu bheil sluagh air a bhith a’ còmhnaidh an seo bho Linn Ùr na Cloiche, còrr is 5000 bliadhna air ais. Tha na gheibh Donnchadh falaichte air cliathaich beinne aig àird 1600 troigh a’ nochdadh gu bheil e air rudeigin a lorg mu ar sinnsearan tràtha a dh’fhaodadh a bhith cudromach aig ìre eadar-nàiseanta.
Local historian and deerstalker Duncan Mackenzie has a passion for unearthing the history of his ancestors in Inverlael Glen. Following on from a successful film in 2022, we follow Duncan as his investigations take a step forward. Newly unearthed written records stretching back to 1370 give a rare insight into early medieval life in rural Scotland, and the scale of this community - 20 square miles - confirms its importance.
Yet it is Duncan’s unrivalled knowledge of these hills and glens that has led to a major breakthrough and the tantalising discovery that people may have lived here since Neolithic times, over 5,000 years ago. What Duncan finds hidden on the mountainside at 1,600 feet suggests he has discovered something about our early ancestors that could be of international importance.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Calum Cille: An Naomh Dana/Columba - The Bold Saint
programme.desc:
He was at the centre of a bloody battle and founded a monastery that became a beacon of civilisation in the Early Middle Ages. He is even said to have taken on the Loch Ness monster. But who was Colmcille, the Irish abbot also known as St Columba? Born in AD 521, his exploits as poet, scribe, politician, warrior and holy man became notorious throughout Ireland and Scotland.
This revealing new documentary, broadcast on the 1500th anniversary of his birth, explores the man, the myth and his legacy today.
Bha e aig teis-mheadhan blàr fuilteach agus stèidhich e manachainn a thàinig gu bhith na solas-iùil sìobhaltais sna Meadhan Aoisean Tràtha. Tha e ri ràdh mu dheidhinn cuideachd gun robh e an sàs ann an Uile-bhèist Loch Nis.
Ach cò a bha ann an Calum Cille, an t-aba Èireannach, a bha aithnichte ann an Alba mar an Naomh Calum Cille? Rugadh e ann an 521RC, agus dh’fhàs e ainmeil air feadh Èirinn agus Alba airson a shaothair mar bhàrd, sgrìobhaiche, neach poilitigs, laoch agus naomh.
Tha am prògram ùr aithriseach seo a chaidh a chraoladh air an là a bha a’ comharrachadh an là a rugadh e o chionn mìle is còig cheud (1500) bliadhna a’ rannsachadh an duine, an sgeula mu dheidhinn agus an dìleab a dh’fhàg e againn. Narrator - Shona Henderson Executive Producer - Seumas Mactaggart Executive Producer - Margaret Cameron Producer - Joanna Young Producer - Keith O'Grady.

programme.title: An Cruinne Caochlaideach/Dynamic Planet
programme.desc:
Tha deigh aig pòlaichean a’ phlanaid agus mullaichean nam beanntan ag atharrachadh gu mòr. Thèid tòrr dheth à sealladh san linn seo. Tha na cruthan-tìre deighe seo a’ dol tro chruth atharrachadh, ach tha buaidh aig an leaghadh a’ dol nas fhaide buileach – chan eil àite sam bith sàbhailte bho na dh’ fhaodadh tachairt.
Fhad ’s a tha uisge reòthte a’ leaghadh bho na h-eigh-shruthan, siotaichean deighe pòlarach agus deigh na mara, tha e ag atharrachadh patarain aimsire agus sruthan mara, agus chan eil an saoghal mar a tha sinne eòlach air cho aithnichte dhuinn.
A’ falbh air turas iongantach bho phòlaichean reòthte an Antartaig agus an Artaig gu àrd-chlàran mòr agus sgurran na Himalayas, tha sgioba sònraichte de eòlaichean a’ tabhainn adhbhar dòchais airson àm ri teachd as aonais deighe. Tha sinn a’ sreap am broinn eigh-shruthan, a’ tighinn faisg air ròin, mucan-mara dhronnach agus mathain bàna gus tuigse fhaighinn air mar a tha beatha agus nàdar ag atharrachadh agus a’ glacadh modhan bheathaichean, nach deach fhaicinn a-riamh, air film.
Tha am prògram seo a’ taisbeanadh mar a tha nàdar a’ lorg dòigh, agus mar a tha saidheans agus traidisean gar ullachadh fhèin agus ar Cruinne Caochlaideach airson àm ri teachd a tha ag atharrachadh aig astar.
Ice at the planet’s poles and mountain peaks is changing drastically. Much will disappear completely this century. These icescapes are transforming, but the impact of the melt goes much further - nowhere on the planet is immune from the sometimes-unexpected consequences. As frozen water melts from glaciers, polar ice caps and sea ice, it changes weather patterns and ocean currents, and the world as we know it.
Journeying from the frozen poles of Antarctica and the Arctic to the vast plateaus and soaring peaks of the Himalayas, an extraordinary team of experts offer hope for a future with less ice.
We climb into glaciers and capture never seen before animal behaviour on film - getting up close with seals, humpback whales and polar bears to understand how life is changing and nature is adapting. This programme reveals how nature finds a way, and how science, and tradition can help prepare us and our Dynamic Planet for a fast-changing future.

Oona and Baba have spotted a dung beetle – a special little creature on an important mission to roll his dung ball back to the nest! The beetle is highly skilled, but there are many obstacles in his way and he may need help from some friends. programme.desc:

Mama has hurt her wing and cannot join Papa on today’s fishing trip. Oona is determined that she will help Papa instead but, between strong winds and menacing seagulls, Oona will need to show just how brave she can be! Aithris - John Carmichael Oona - Zoe Drysdale Baba - Adam Kaiess Mama - Ellen MacDonald Papa - Calum Macaulay Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Ishbel Maclean Singer - Zoe Drysdale.

programme.title: Fillte
programme.desc:
Continuing a journey throughout Scotland to discover the historic and contemporary hand-crafted practices behind artisan producers of woven fabrics. These include wool, hemp, linen, grasses, leather, and many more unorthodox fabrics.
Tha Fillte a gabhail turas tro Alba a’ sireadh eachdraidh agus sgeulachdan an latha ’n diugh co-cheangailte ris an luchd-ciùird a tha snìomh ‘s ag obrachadh diofar stuthan, leithid, clòimh, corcach, anart, feur,leathar, agus iomadh seorsa stuth iongantach eile.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc:
Tha Joy Dunlop gar toirt tro na ciad ceumannan a tha a dhìth airson ar misneachadh gus Gàidhlig a bhruidhinn. Thairis air an t-sreath, bidh i a’ dèiligeadh ri facail is abairtean air measgachadh de chuspairean co-cheangailte ri gach taobh de ar beatha. Leis gun do dh’ionnsaich i fhèin, bheir Joy dhuinn briathrachas mu charaidean, an dachaigh, an teaghlach, obair agus an aimsir am measg gu leòr eile ann an dòigh a tha sìmplidh agus furasta a thuigsinn. Bidh stiùireadh ann cuideachd a thaobh a bhith a’ cleachdadh abairtean, le eisimpleirean soilleir ann an dramathan goirid.
Coinnichidh sinn luchd-ionnsachaidh èasgaidh, feadhainn a tha ag ionnsachadh as ùr agus cuid a bha fileanta agus a sguir ga cleachdadh, agus iadsan a th’ air a bhith ag ionnsachadh fad bhliadhnaichean. Agus bidh Calum MacIlleathain a’ toirt sealladh eile dhuinn air Alba is e ann an diofar àitichean air feadh na dùthcha.
Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne: www.speakgaelic.scot agus ann an sreath phodcastan a tha ri fhaighinn air BBC Sounds.
Joy Dunlop guides viewers through the first steps to inspire us to speak Gaelic. Throughout the series, she introduces words and phrases on a variety of everyday topics. A Gaelic learner herself, Joy supports us through pronunciation and vocabulary on topics such as friends, family, home, work and weather.
We meet diligent learners who have embraced speaking Gaelic, from new learners to lapsed native speakers and the on-off learners who have improved their language skills over the decades. And, the intrepid Calum Maclean takes us on adventures to hidden treasures around Scotland.
Supporting materials can be found online: www.speakgaelic.scot and in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds. Presenter - Joy Dunlop Presenter - Calum Maclean Executive Producer - Una McDonald Producer - Colin MacLeod.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc:
Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc:
Seo an fharpais-cheist far a bheil barrachd air eòlas coitcheann a dhìth gus buannachadh. Le Niall Iain Dòmnhallach aig an stiùir cluichidh na sgiobaidhean anns an stiùideo an aghaidh an ochdnar Mas Fhìoraich a tha a’ cluich bhon dachaighean fhèin agus a tha a’ cur nan ceistean. A’ strì an aghaidh na Mas Fhìoraich airson feuchainn air an duais mhòr, tha Joshua is Lewis, agus Anna is Eve.
Presented by Niall Iain MacDonald, this is the quiz show where more than general knowledge is required to win. Playing from the comfort of their own homes are the Pretenders, and they are the ones posing the questions. Battling the Pretenders to win the big prize are Joshua and Lewis, and Anna and Eve.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Eòrpa
programme.desc: Eòrpa reports on some of the most important issues from Scotland and across Europe.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc:
Thathar ag ràdh gur e na ficheadan na bliadhnaichean as fheàrr a bhios agad nad bheatha, ach dè cho eadar-dhealaichte ’s a tha e a bhith anns na ficheadan an-dràsta an coimeas ri deich no fichead bliadhna air ais? Agus dè mu dhèidhinn bho chionn ceud bliadhna?Bho rugadh iad san linn ditseatach, tha an ginealach seo air am meas mar dhaoine aig a bheil barrachd mothachadh sòisealta, a tha nas fhallain agus nas fheàrr dhan àrainneachd na ginealaichean a chaidh air thoiseach orra. Thathas a’ faighneachd dhaibh dè na cuspairean a tha a’ cur dragh orra agus mu ciamar a tha gach duine aca a’ gluasad tro am beatha.
Tha Cass Ezeji a tha 29 a’ coinneachadh ri measgachadh de dhaoine a th’ anns na ficheadan gus faighinn a-mach cò ris a tha e dha rìribh coltach agus tha i a’ faighneachd ciamar a tha iad a’ faireachdainn mun t-saoghal mu thimcheall orra. Am measg eile, tha i a’ coinneachadh ri Mark Mac a’ Ghobhainn à Eilean Leòdhais a tha a-nis a’ fuireach ann an Glaschu, a tha èasgaidh mu bhith a’ brosnachadh Gàidhlig air na meadhanan sòisealta ’s Iona NicIlleBhàin a tha a’ faireachdainn gu bheil e deatamach dòigh-beatha seasmhach a leantainn agus a tha ag aithneachadh atharrachadh na gnàth shìde mar chuspair air leth cudromach. Prògram beòthail, dathach le measgachadh de ghuthan òg, làidir.
Your twenties are said to be the best years of your life, but how different is it to be in your twenties now in comparison to ten or 20 years back- or even a century ago? Born into the digital age, the current twentysomethings are seen to be more socially aware, health-conscious and environmentally responsible than previous generations. They are asked what issues matter to them and how they are navigating life through their twenties.
Cass Ezeji, who is 29, meets a variety of young people to find out what life is really like and asks how they feel about the constantly evolving world around them. Mark Smith, from the Isle of Lewis and now living in Glasgow, is enthusiastic about promoting the Gaelic language on social media platforms, while Iona Whyte is extremely passionate about a sustainable way of living and recognises climate change as an important issue. A lively and colourful programme with a diverse selection of strong and youthful voices.

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.sub-title: An t-Eagal, An t-Eudach ‘s An Gaol – Fear, Envy and Love ║ S1E5/6
programme.desc:
Murdina is thrown into turmoil when she realises that Johan is becoming a majority shareholder in the mill. Manager Sìleas offers newcomer Rory a job as one of the drivers. But just who exactly is this mysterious Irish stranger, Rory? Ivor and Dòmhnall’s relationship is put to the test when Ivor shares his fears that he may be responsible for the fire.
Tha Murdina troimhe-chèile nuair a tha i ag ionnsachadh gur ann aig Johan a bhios an roinn as motha ‘sa mhuileann. Tha Sìleas, ceannard na muilne, a’ toirt obair do Rory mar dhraibhear, ‘s e air ùr nochdadh. Ach cò dìreach a th’ anns a’ choigreach Èireannach, Rory? Tha buaireadh eadar Ivor is Dòmhnall, le Ivor ag aideachadh gur dòcha gur esan as coireach airson an teine.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Seumas - Ewen MacKinnon Sileas - Erica Morrison Donald - Eoghan MacDonald Murdina - Emma MacLeod Shonnie - David MacKenzie Executive Producer - Jim Webster Executive Producer - Tony Kearney.

programme.title: Am Balla (The Wall)
programme.desc:
Leth-cheud bliadhna às deidh deireadh Cogadh, tha Ramsay MacMahon a’ dol air turas gus faighinn a-mach mar a tha an cogadh agus sgaradh na dùthcha fhathast a’ toirt buaidh air daoine ann am Bhietnam an-diugh. Tro thuras, chì Ramsay seann shaighdearan bhon dà thaobh a tha a’ tighinn aghaidh ri aghaidh airson a’ chiad uair bho thàinig an cogadh gu crìoch. Thèid e a-mach còmhla ri sgiobaidhean a tha ag obair gus bomaichean is mèinnean nach deach an spreadhadh a thoirt às an talamh; agus cluinnidh e sgeulachdan mu dhaoine a tha fhathast beò le buaidh cogadh le stuthan ceimigeach.
Half a century after the end of the Vietnam War and the country's reunification, Ramsay MacMahon embarks on a journey to discover how war and division continue to affect people in Vietnam today. During his journey, Ramsay meets former soldiers from both sides who come face to face with each other for the first time since the war ended. He joins teams working to clear unexploded ordnance from the ground; and he hears the stories of people still living with the consequences of chemical warfare.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Vets: Gach Creutair Beo
programme.desc:
Anns an t-sreath seo coinnichidh sinn ri lighichean-sprèidh bho air feadh Alba is iad ri frithealadh iomadach seòrsa beathach beag is mòr, peatail agus fiadhaich. Bidh sgeulachdan toileachais agus bròin pailt agus sinn a’ coinneachadh ris gach creutair beò.
An t-seachdain-sa, ann an Siorrachd Obar Dheathain, tha Scott Rigg a’ dèanamh obair-lannsa air spòg tarbh-chù Frangach airson droch lùbadh na spòg dheiridh a cheartachadh.
Airson a’ chiad uair, tha Scott a’ cleachdadh iùilean is cumaidhean a chaidh an dèanamh a dh'aona ghnothaich dhan chù seo, a' cleachdadh clò-bhualadair 3D. Aig Pàirc Fiadh-Bheatha na Gàidhealtachd, ‘s e latha a’ bhanachdaich a th’ ann dha piseagan cait-fhiadhaich, ach chan eil iad idir furasta an làimhseachadh. Agus, tha David Buckland trang ann an Uibhist a Deas le caora aig àm breith nan uan
Scott Rigg operates on a French bulldog in Aberdeenshire to correct a severe bend in his leg, with the help of some new technology. This is the first time Scott has used a series of guides and templates during surgery that have been custom made for the dog using a 3D printer.
At Highland Wildlife Park, Jane Harley is vaccinating some feisty wildcat kittens, and David Buckland has his hands full in South Uist with a tricky lambing.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.sub-title: An t-Àite-obrach ║ S2(A2)E7/13. The Workplace ║ S2(A2)E7/13
programme.desc:
Tha Joy Dunlop gar toirt tro na h-ath cheumannan airson ar misneachadh gus leantainn oirnn a bhith bruidhinn na Gàidhlig. Thairis air an t-sreath seo, bidh i a’ dèiligeadh ri facail is abairtean air measgachadh de chuspairean co-cheangailte ri gach taobh de ar beatha. Leis gun do dh’ionnsaich i fhèin, bheir Joy dhuinn briathrachas a tha sìmplidh agus furasta a thuigsinn. Bidh stiùireadh ann cuideachd a thaobh a bhith a’ cleachdadh abairtean, le eisimpleirean soilleir tro chòmhraidhean goirid.
Coinnichidh sinn ri luchd-ionnsachaidh èasgaidh, feadhainn a tha ag ionnsachadh as ùr, cuid a bha fileanta ’s a sguir ga cleachdadh agus iadsan a th’ air a bhith ag ionnsachadh fad bhliadhnaichean. Agus bidh Calum MacIlleathain a’ toirt sealladh eile dhuinn air Alba is e ann an diofar àiteachan air feadh na dùthcha.Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne aig www.speakgaelic.scot agus ann an sreath phodcastan air BBC Sounds.
Joy Dunlop guides viewers through the next steps to inspire us to speak Gaelic. Throughout the series, she introduces words and phrases on a variety of everyday topics. A Gaelic learner herself, Joy supports us through pronunciation and vocabulary on topics such as friends, home, work and communication.
We meet diligent learners who have embraced speaking Gaelic, from new learners to lapsed native speakers and the on-off learners who have improved their language skills over the decades. And, the intrepid Calum Maclean takes us on adventures to hidden treasures around Scotland.
Supporting materials can be found online at www.speakgaelic.scot and in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds. Presenter - Joy Dunlop Executive Producer - Una MacDonald.

programme.title: Immigration Tracks
programme.desc:
From Canada's eastern province of Cape Breton, we make our way on a journey to Toronto, Ontario, in search of Scottish Gaelic families who made a new life in this vast country over 100 years ago. In this episode, we head from Cape Breton to Nova Scotia. Finding a home away from home, we visit Baile nan Gàidheal. How do generations of Scots identify with their roots? Join Anne MacAlpine on a cultural voyage of discovery.
Bho Cheap Breatainn sa cheann an ear de Chanada, tha sinn a’ togail oirnn air slighe-rathaid chun an iar, gu ruige Toronto, Ontario. A’ sireadh theaghlaichean Gàidhlig a rinn beatha ùr dhaibh fhèin san dùthaich mhòr seo còrr air ceud bliadhna air ais.
San earrann seo, tha sinn a’ siubhal à Ceap Breatainn gu Alba Nuadh agus a' dol a thadhal air a’ mhuseum dhùthchasach – Baile nan Gàidheal.
Thig còmhla ri Anne NicAilpein air an turas chultural seo is i a’ feuchainn ri faighinn a-mach dè seòrsa ceangal a th’ aig Canèideanaich Albannach rim freumhan? Presenter - Anne MacAlpine Director - Calum Angus Mackay Producer - Rachel Ellen Mackay Editor - Paul Duke.

programme.title: Cùram
programme.desc:
Sreath ùr cumhachdach mu gaisgich cùraim, a tha a’ comharrachadh an neart, a’ cho-fhaireachdainn, agus cho làidir ’s a tha an luchd-cùraim fhèin agus an fheadhainn aig a bheil feum air cùram air feadh na h-Eileanan an Iar de dh’ Alba.
Le còrr air trì mìle luchd-cùraim nach eil a’ faighinn taic airgid air feadh coimhearsnachdan eileanach – bho Leòdhas chun na Hearadh gu na h-Eileanan a Deas – tha na prògraman seo a’ toirt guth don fheadhainn a tha a’ toirt seachad agus an fheadhainn a tha a’ faighinn cùram gach là. Ma ’s ann a’ gabhail cùram airson neach-dèiligidh, pàrant, no ball teaghlaich, tha na daoine seo a’ toirt seachad cùram fad-bheatha, cùram ann an seann-aois, no taic airson feumalachdan cùraim a tha a’ tighinn an uair nach eil dùil ris, gun mòran aithneachadh agus gun mòran ghoireasan.
Le duilgheadasan ionmhais agus cuideam air luchd-obrach, tha an roinn cùraim nas cleachdte ri càineadh agus gearain, ach tha luchd-obrach anns gach ceàrnaidh a tha ag obair cruaidh airson an taic as fheàrr a thoirt seachad, gu math tric còmhla ri teaghlaichean.
A series which shines the light on unseen care heroes. It pays tribute and celebrates the quiet strength, compassion and resilience of carers and those living with care needs across the Western Isles of Scotland.
With over 3,000 unpaid carers spread across the island communities, from Lewis and Harris to the Southern Isles, we give voice to the experiences of those who provide and receive care every single day. Whether caring for a client, parent or other family member, these individuals offer essential support for lifelong, ageing or unexpected care needs, often with little recognition and few resources.
Plagued with financial and staffing stress, the care sector is more used to criticism and complaint. But there are workers in every area who go above and beyond to try and deliver the best support they can, often in tandem with family networks.
In the first episode, we meet Donald John Maclean from Sollas in North Uist who has cerebral palsy.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Director - David Martin Editor - Calum Blane Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Editor - Courtney Gillies Producer - Ann Morrison.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc:
Thathar ag ràdh gur e na ficheadan na bliadhnaichean as fheàrr a bhios agad nad bheatha, ach dè cho eadar-dhealaichte ’s a tha e a bhith anns na ficheadan an-dràsta an coimeas ri deich no fichead bliadhna air ais? Agus dè mu dhèidhinn bho chionn ceud bliadhna?Bho rugadh iad san linn ditseatach, tha an ginealach seo air am meas mar dhaoine aig a bheil barrachd mothachadh sòisealta, a tha nas fhallain agus nas fheàrr dhan àrainneachd na ginealaichean a chaidh air thoiseach orra. Thathas a’ faighneachd dhaibh dè na cuspairean a tha a’ cur dragh orra agus mu ciamar a tha gach duine aca a’ gluasad tro am beatha.
Tha Cass Ezeji a tha 29 a’ coinneachadh ri measgachadh de dhaoine a th’ anns na ficheadan gus faighinn a-mach cò ris a tha e dha rìribh coltach agus tha i a’ faighneachd ciamar a tha iad a’ faireachdainn mun t-saoghal mu thimcheall orra. Am measg eile, tha i a’ coinneachadh ri Mark Mac a’ Ghobhainn à Eilean Leòdhais a tha a-nis a’ fuireach ann an Glaschu, a tha èasgaidh mu bhith a’ brosnachadh Gàidhlig air na meadhanan sòisealta ’s Iona NicIlleBhàin a tha a’ faireachdainn gu bheil e deatamach dòigh-beatha seasmhach a leantainn agus a tha ag aithneachadh atharrachadh na gnàth shìde mar chuspair air leth cudromach. Prògram beòthail, dathach le measgachadh de ghuthan òg, làidir.
Your twenties are said to be the best years of your life, but how different is it to be in your twenties now in comparison to ten or 20 years back- or even a century ago? Born into the digital age, the current twentysomethings are seen to be more socially aware, health-conscious and environmentally responsible than previous generations. They are asked what issues matter to them and how they are navigating life through their twenties.
Cass Ezeji, who is 29, meets a variety of young people to find out what life is really like and asks how they feel about the constantly evolving world around them. Mark Smith, from the Isle of Lewis and now living in Glasgow, is enthusiastic about promoting the Gaelic language on social media platforms, while Iona Whyte is extremely passionate about a sustainable way of living and recognises climate change as an important issue. A lively and colourful programme with a diverse selection of strong and youthful voices.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc:

programme.title: Greim-Bìdh le Gregor
programme.desc:
Gregor MacLeod is passionate about local produce. From his home on the Isle of Lewis, he shows us the people and places he goes to for the finest ingredients.
In Stornoway, Gregor visits the last place on the island to make kippers. There he lends a hand before taking his prized produce home to cook up Spanish-inspired kipper croquettes with home-made mayonnaise.
Gregor is the proud owner of 16 chickens who provide him with eggs aplenty. This often means a glut of fresh eggs. Gregor shows us how he puts them to good use in his showstopping pavlova tower. 'Waste not, want not' is his motto, so he turns the remaining yolks into a bright purple bramble curd to go between each layer of marshmallow pavlova.
Something sweet to accompany a coffee is a must. Gregor is a trained barista, so to go with his flat white he makes wafer twirl biscuits dipped in chocolate and hazelnuts.
Tha Gregor MacLeòid dealasach mu bhiadh ionadail. Bho dhachaigh ann an Leòdhas, tha e a’ sealltainn dhuinn na daoine agus na h-àiteachan gum bi e a’ dol airson a’ bhìdh as fheàrr.
Tha Gregor ann an Steòrnabhagh ag ionnsachadh mu bhith a’ dèanamh chioparan. A’ tilleadh dhachaigh, tha e a’ dèanamh croquettes chioparan le dreach Spàinneach is am mayo aige fhèin.
Tha Gregor gu math pròiseil mu na 16 cearcan a tha ga sholarachadh le pailteas uighean. Tha e a’ sealltainn dhuinn mar a tha e gan cuir gu feum anns an tùr phabhlòbha iongantach aige. Gus nach tèid càil a dhìth, tha e a’ cleachdadh nam buidheagan a th’ air fhàgail airson curd soileir-purpaidh a dhèanamh le smeuran. Thèid seo eadar gach filleadh dhen phabhlòbha.Feumar rudeigin milis le cofaidh. Tha Gregor a’ dèanamh briosgaidean uafair air am bogadh ann an teòclaid is cnòthan-calltainn airson a ghabhail le flat white.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Clutha
programme.desc:
10 bliadhna às deidh tubaist anns an do bhuail heileacoptair poileis ann an taigh-seinnse, a’ Chlutha, ann an Glaschu, tha cuimhneachain thiamhaidh mar fhianais air oidhche dhorcha a dh’fhàg làrach mhaireannach air a’ bhaile.
Ten years on from the accident that saw a police helicopter crash into Glasgow pub, The Clutha, eyewitnesses and emergency services share moving testimonies. A dark night that left an indelible mark on the city.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Dàna
Scotland's Wild Side
programme.sub-title: An Spàinn ║ Dàna. S4. AnRoinn-EòrpaE3/5. Costa Blanca ║ Dàna. S4. AnRoinn-EòrpaE3/5
programme.desc:
Tha ceangal làidir aig an sgìre Costa Blanca san Spàinn ri saor-làithean is luchd-turais a’ sireadh na grèine, ach tha Coinneach MacFhraing a’ faighinn a-mach gu bheil an sgìre seo a’ tabhann sreap air leth don neach-siubhal as Dàna. Còmhla ris a’ chompanach sreap, Somhairle Mac Iain, tha Coinneach a’ cur seachad ùine ann an aon de na cinn-uidhe turasachd as motha san Roinn Eòrpa agus a’ tighinn tarsaing air dùbhlain inntinneach air a’ bhlàr a-muigh, air falbh bho ghleadhraich Baile Benidorm.
While Spain’s Costa Blanca may be more closely associated with package holidays than with adventure sports, Coinneach Rankin finds that the area offers incredible climbing to the more intrepid holidaymaker. Along with climbing partner, Somhairle Johnston, Coinneach explores one of Europe’s most popular tourist destinations and discovers thrilling challenges, a world apart from the bustle of Benidorm.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Coinneach Rankin Executive Producer - Tony Kearney Executive Producer - Jim Webster Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Director - Hamish MacLeod Producer - Rowan Green.

programme.title: Ro Thrath don t-Saoghal/Born too Soon
programme.desc:
Tha Daisy a’ faighinn leigheas èiginneach agus i a’ strì ri a h-anail a tharraing, fhad ’s a tha Treasa agus Ian a’ cur fàilte air na leth-aoin aca agus gan ullachadh fhèin airson Joshua a chall. Tha piseach a’ tighinn air Diane, agus thèid Méabh a ghluasad nas fhaisge air a dachaigh.
Daisy receives emergency treatment for severe breathing problems, while Treasa and Ian welcome their twins and prepare to lose Joshua. Diane makes progress, and Méabh is transferred closer to home.
Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.sub-title: Carach neo caireachd/The Kung Phew Challenge ║ S2E7/10
programme.desc:
Tha am baile na thàmh agus a h-uile duine air cruinneachadh ann an talla - bhaile, feuch co a gheibh làmh an uachdar air a sgioba caireachd a th' air a' thighinn a cheilidh.
The town is deserted as everybody is at the town hall, where a visiting wrestling troupe has laid down the gauntlet to the locals. Who will win the day?

programme.title: Faodail: Beatha nan Eilean (Shorts)
programme.desc:
Footage from the Faodail. Found Film Archive of the Outer Hebrides from the 1930s to the 1980s, charting growing up in the islands. The strong community ties of past generations still influence the islands today.

In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.sub-title: An t-Eagal, An t-Eudach ‘s An Gaol – Fear, Envy and Love ║ S1E5/6
programme.desc:
Murdina is thrown into turmoil when she realises that Johan is becoming a majority shareholder in the mill. Manager Sìleas offers newcomer Rory a job as one of the drivers. But just who exactly is this mysterious Irish stranger, Rory? Ivor and Dòmhnall’s relationship is put to the test when Ivor shares his fears that he may be responsible for the fire.
Tha Murdina troimhe-chèile nuair a tha i ag ionnsachadh gur ann aig Johan a bhios an roinn as motha ‘sa mhuileann. Tha Sìleas, ceannard na muilne, a’ toirt obair do Rory mar dhraibhear, ‘s e air ùr nochdadh. Ach cò dìreach a th’ anns a’ choigreach Èireannach, Rory? Tha buaireadh eadar Ivor is Dòmhnall, le Ivor ag aideachadh gur dòcha gur esan as coireach airson an teine.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Seumas - Ewen MacKinnon Sileas - Erica Morrison Donald - Eoghan MacDonald Murdina - Emma MacLeod Shonnie - David MacKenzie Executive Producer - Jim Webster Executive Producer - Tony Kearney.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc:
Nuair a tha Bing is Sula a’ peantadh sa ghàrradh, tha tubaist ann leis an uisg’ is tha e a’ dòrtadh air falbh. Tha Bing an uairsin a’ tionndadh na pìob-uisg’ air ro luath agus tha coltas nathair oillteil air an uisge.
As Bing and Sula paint in the garden, the water is knocked over accidentally. Bing then tries to get fresh water using the hosepipe, but it looks like a scary snake when he turns it on too quickly. programme.title: Bing
programme.desc:

Bing is not happy when Pando doesn’t do things the same way as he does at his birthday party. Fortunately, Flop is on hand to show that it is fine when people do things differently to him. programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc:
Tha Ben agus na h-Abadas a' cluich an Geama Fhaclan a-rithist, agus tha aon dhaibh a' dol a lorg creutair tha beò fon t-uisge le slige air a dhruim - turtur-mara. Cò'n t-Abadas a b'fheàrr airson turtur-mara a lorg?
Ben joins the Abadas for the word game and soon one of them goes searching for a creature that lives underwater and has a shell on its back - a sea turtle. Which of the Abadas would be the best one to search for the sea turtle?

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.sub-title: Eilean Fad air Falbh/Far away Island ║ CleasanAtaidh&Tilidh/TheAdventures/Abney&TealS1E15/52
programme.desc:
Tha Tilidh a’ falbh a dh’fhaicinn cò ris a bhiodh e coltach fuireach air eilean fad air falbh. Tha Àtaidh draghail gum bi i aonranach, mar sin tha e a’ cur nam Boga-bogadach thuice, ach nuair a ruigeas iad, tha aonan air a dhol a dhìth sa phost!
Teal goes to see what it’s like living on a far away island. Abney worries that she might be lonely and sends her the Poc-Pocs for company, but when they arrive there is one missing - lost in the post! programme.desc:

programme.title: Seonaidh
Shaun the Sheep
programme.sub-title: Poidsear Ping Pong ║ Seonaidh. S4E28/30. Ping-Pong Poacher ║ Seonaidh. S4E28/30
programme.desc:

With the animals of Mossybottom Farm keenly watching Shaun v Bitzer in the greatest table tennis match of all time, they fail to notice a hungry fox who isn't keeping his eye on the ball at all.

programme.desc:
Dè a tha ag adhbharachadh am bùrach san rùm aig Flòraidh? Agus cò a shiolp an leabhar aig Flòraidh? Saoil a bheil gnothaich aig taibhs’ ris?
What has caused the mess in Flòraidh’s room? And who has stolen Flòraidh’s book? Does a ghost have anything to do with this? Hilda - Mischa Macpherson Flòraidh (Frida) - Lauren Macdonald Daibhidh (David) - Ellen MacDonald Artair (Alfur) - Derek MacIntosh Flòraidh's Mum - Ceitlin Lilidh Executive Producer - Bill MacLeod Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Alec MacDonald.

programme.title: Vets: Gach Creutair Beo
programme.desc:
Anns an t-sreath seo coinnichidh sinn ri lighichean-sprèidh bho air feadh Alba is iad ri frithealadh iomadach seòrsa beathach beag is mòr, peatail agus fiadhaich. Bidh sgeulachdan toileachais agus bròin pailt agus sinn a’ coinneachadh ris gach creutair beò.
An t-seachdain-sa, ann an Siorrachd Obar Dheathain, tha Scott Rigg a’ dèanamh obair-lannsa air spòg tarbh-chù Frangach airson droch lùbadh na spòg dheiridh a cheartachadh.
Airson a’ chiad uair, tha Scott a’ cleachdadh iùilean is cumaidhean a chaidh an dèanamh a dh'aona ghnothaich dhan chù seo, a' cleachdadh clò-bhualadair 3D. Aig Pàirc Fiadh-Bheatha na Gàidhealtachd, ‘s e latha a’ bhanachdaich a th’ ann dha piseagan cait-fhiadhaich, ach chan eil iad idir furasta an làimhseachadh. Agus, tha David Buckland trang ann an Uibhist a Deas le caora aig àm breith nan uan
Scott Rigg operates on a French bulldog in Aberdeenshire to correct a severe bend in his leg, with the help of some new technology. This is the first time Scott has used a series of guides and templates during surgery that have been custom made for the dog using a 3D printer.
At Highland Wildlife Park, Jane Harley is vaccinating some feisty wildcat kittens, and David Buckland has his hands full in South Uist with a tricky lambing.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc:
Tha Joy Dunlop a’ leantainn oirre ’s i gar toirt tro cheumannan a bharrachd ann a bhith ag ionnsachadh na Gàidhlig. Bidh i a’ dèiligeadh ri facail is abairtean air measgachadh de chuspairean làitheil agus, mar thè a dh’ionnsaich na Gàidhlig i fhèin, bheir Joy mìneachadh dhuinn air briathrachas, gràmar is gnathasan-cainnte ann an dòigh a tha furasta a thuigsinn.
Coinnichidh sinn ri luchd-labhairt èasgaidh a th’ air Gàidhlig ionnsachadh gu àrd ìre neo a thogadh leis a’ Ghàidhlig air falbh bho sgìrean traidiseanta na Gàidhealtachd, agus bidh Calum MacIlleathain a’ toirt sealladh dhuinn air annasan is cuspairean ’s e air chuairt air feadh na dùthcha.
Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne aig www.speakgaelic.scot, ann am pod-chraolaidhean SpeakGaelic air BBC Sounds agus tha na prògraman air fad rin lorg le fo-thiotalan air sianal YouTube SpeakGaelic.
Joy Dunlop guides viewers through the next steps to inspire us to keep on speaking Gaelic. As in previous series, she introduces and explains usage for words and phrases on everyday topics. A Gaelic learner herself, Joy supports us through vocabulary, grammar and idiom on topics such as medicine, politics, community and exercise.
We meet diligent speakers who have embraced the language, and the intrepid Calum Maclean ventures to forgotten corners of Scotland seeking hidden treasures.
Supporting materials can be found online: www.speakgaelic.scot, in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds and with English subtitles on SpeakGaelic’s YouTube channel. Presenter - Joy Dunlop Presenter - Calum Maclean Producer - Donald Macleod Executive Producer - Una McDonald.

programme.title: Port An Obain
programme.desc:
Baile an Òbain….prìomh bhaile Earra Ghàidheal is Bhòid..cala trang gach latha dhen bhliadhna….le soithichean obrach ..aiseagan beaga, is mòra, uile a’ frithealadh gach duine tha fuireach anns an sgìre. Gu leòr eile tha tighinn a chèilidh air a’ bhaile…air trèana, bus, neo air seòl… tha an t-Òban aithnichte mar aon de na prìomh bhailtean Albannach do luchd-turais….biadh mara sònraichte, agus blas traidiseanta air gach nì eile tha’s a’ tamhainn dha na mìltean a th’ air saor-làithean…..ach se cuideachd àite obrach a th’ ann…. ….muir a’ toirt beò-shlàinte do chuid a tha fuireach anns na h-eileannan eireachdail a tha a’ cuairteachadh na sgìre, ….a dh’aindeoin aimsir neo ràithaichean
Oban is the main town of Argyll and Bute. It's a busy port 365 days a year, with workboats and ferries of all sizes attending to the needs of the local population. Oban is an increasingly popular destination with tourists - who arrive by train, bus or under sail - offering exceptional seafood and a very traditional holiday experience for the many thousands of visitors to enjoy. But it is also a place of work. The sea provides a living for some who reside in beautiful islands located throughout the Argyll area, where work continues despite the weather or the season.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ro Thrath don t-Saoghal/Born too Soon
programme.desc:
Tha leigheas a dhìth air na leth-aoin Hughie agus Brodie an dèidh dhaibh a bhith air am breith ro thràth. Tha Joshua air a bhaisteadh mus eil e, gu brònach, a’ bàsachadh. Tha lannsa cridhe a dhìth air Méabh agus tha leanaban Siobhán a’ tighinn tràth.
Twin boys Hughie and Brodie need life-saving treatment after being born prematurely. Joshua is baptised and sadly passes away. Méabh needs heart surgery, and Siobhán’s baby is delivered early.
Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.sub-title: De a tha gluasad 's a choille?/If you go into the woods today.. ║ S2E8/10
programme.desc:
Tha Ina is Seasaidh feumach air ùrachadh agus tha iad a' togail oirre air chuairt. Ach tha rudan neònach a' feitheamh oirre anns a choille.
Ina and Jessie want to recharge their batteries and head off on holiday, but strange goings-on in the woods result in a very different set of holiday snaps.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc:
Tha trèat sònraicht' aig Abigail, trèat ùr agus blasta de Fhritearan Mearag-bheag agus Peasair. Fèir ceart 'son a bhith air bòrd lòin air no bòrd bruinse, nuair a tha an teaghlach no caraidean ri tadhal.
Abigail has a special treat in store in the form of fresh and tasty courgette and pea fritters. It's perfect for adding to that table top brunch or lunch spread when family or friends are visiting.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Abigail Maciver Producer - Kenneth Stewart Production Manager - Mairi Macleod Executive Producer - Rachel Ellen Mackay.

programme.title: Glan Fhèin
programme.desc:
Tha na seann charaidean Katie agus Angela a’ stiùireadh companaidh glanaidh a bhios a’ seirbhiseachadh thaighean air mhàl geàrr-ùine gu h-àraidh. Tha an gnìomhachas air leth soirbheachail agus tha sùil aig Lewis Friseal, a tha na entrepreneur ionadail agus na chomhairliche spèiseail, anns a’ chompanaidh. Aig an aon àm, tha Betty a’ taisbeanadh bàrdachd a tha brosnaichte le peataichean agus i a’ gabhail ri call pearsanta. Le Dido a’ dèanamh air an ospadal gus leanabh a bhreith, tha Daniel a’ dèanamh beagan matamataig air leatromachd leantaileach. An dàrna sreath den sit-com fhèillmhor le Hannah McKirdy agus Lana Pheutan mar chleasaichean agus sgrìobhaichean.
Old pals Katie and Angela run a cleaning company that specialises in servicing short-term lets. Business is booming and local entrepreneur and esteemed councillor Lewis Fraser has the company in his sights.
Meanwhile, Betty performs pet-inspired poetry as she comes to terms with a personal loss. As Dido rushes to the hospital to give birth, Daniel does the maths on extended long-term pregnancy. Second series of the hit sitcom written by and starring Hannah McKirdy and Lana Pheutan.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Eòrpa
programme.desc: Eòrpa reports on some of the most important issues from Scotland and across Europe.

programme.title: An t-Uisge/Rain Stories
programme.sub-title: Luach An Uisge/The Value of Rain ║ Ant-Uisge/RainStoriesS1E3/3
programme.desc:
Anns an treas prògram, tha sinn a’ rannsachadh uisge mar bhathar luachmhor, a tha a’ cuideachadh ann a bhith a’ toirt cumadh air an eaconamaidh agus a tha toirt buaidh air ar beatha.
Tha Rajendra Singh aithnichte mar Fear Uisge nan Innseachan. Le bhith ag ath-bheòthachadh seann dhòigh air uisge a bhuain, tha e air coimhearsnachdan a chuideachadh le bhith a’ beathachadh talmhainn lom. Tha Singh a’ creidsinn gur ann aig ìre ionadail a-mhàin a ’s urrainnear na toraidhean seo a choileanadh.
Bidh Anne a’ siubhal gu Rubha àlainn na Comraich, far a bheil tòrr uisge air a’ choimhearsnachd iomallach seo a chuideachadh an t-àm ri teachd a dhìon dhaibh pèin, ann a bhith a’ cruthachadh sgeama dealain-uisge.
Agus ann an Sìona, tha sinn a’ faicinn cleachdaidhean uisge sean ’s ùr. Bho Bharraidean-talmhainn Rìs Honghe Hani – far a bheil muinntir Hani a’ stiùireadh siostam toinnte gus an t-uisge aca a chruinneachadh, a th’ air a bhith timcheall mìle bliadhna – gu na bailtean ùra “spuinnse” air an dealbhachadh gus uisge a bharrachd a chùmhnadh.
Le pàtrain uisge a’ fàs nas mì-chinntich, ciamar a tha sinn a’ dèanamh a’ chuid as fheàrr leis an nì as prìseile a th’ againn?
We explore rain as a valuable commodity, which helps shape economies and impacts all our lives. Rajendra Singh is known as the Water Man of India. By reviving an ancient rain harvesting method, he has helped communities regenerate once arid landscapes. Singh believes these kinds of results can only be achieved on a local level.
Anne travels to the stunning Applecross Peninsula where abundant rainfall has helped this remote community ensure its own future with the creation of a hydro scheme.
And in China we witness rain practices old and new. From the Honghe Hani Rice Terraces - where for 1000 years the Hani people have managed an intricate system to harvest their rainwater - to the modern “sponge” cities. Presenter - Anne Lundon Series Producer - Huw Maredudd Director - David Martin Executive Producer - Margaret Cameron Executive Producer - Seumas Mactaggart Executive Producer - Proinsias Ni Ghrainne Executive Producer - Michael Fanning.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries

When a burnt-out delivery van is discovered on a quiet rural road, Rose and Raj are met with a grim crime scene: a charred body in the passenger seat and no sign of the driver. Sifting through the ashes, they uncover a bizarre assortment of clues, including a melted key fob, rusted gardening tools and a bottle of imported Polish vodka.
Tracking down the van’s insured drivers leads them to Kelly Prudham, a tight-lipped agency cleaner, and Scott Smith, a devoted widowed father missing since the previous evening. However, Rose’s sharp eyes spot an identical bottle of Polish vodka in Kelly’s flat, indicating that Kelly may have a dangerous motive for concealing her and Scott’s recent movements.
Meanwhile, Joe can’t resist probing into the mystery. Dragging Brother Christopher along, he snoops around the crime scene and dives into Scott’s past. Relying on his sharp human intuition and feeling somewhat aligned with this man who seems to be struggling as a father, Joe forms a bold theory about Scott’s whereabouts. But his covert search goes sideways, stranding Joe and Christopher in a perilous predicament deep in the Northumbrian moors.
With time running out and danger escalating, Rose, Joe and Raj must pool their findings to identify the burnt remains, track down the arsonist and expose the motive behind the blaze before the truth burns out completely. programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc:
With exclusive access to the police service on the paradise island of Bermuda, we follow life on the front line for the near 400 officers keeping both holidaymakers and locals safe. From patrols and traffic operations to the drug unit, forensics, tactical response teams, the coastguard and community policing, the series goes behind the scenes with the officers at the heart of the action.
The island has its fair share of challenges on both land and sea, with more than 3,000 crimes committed each year. We show how these dedicated officers, including around 30 from the UK, deal with the highs and lows of policing this British Overseas Territory.
In the centre of the island, Sergeant Milton Hill responds to reports of an elderly man walking along a busy roadside in clear distress. When he arrives, the man is unable to recall his name, address or basic personal details, and the mystery begins. Concerned for his safety, Milton stays close, guiding traffic around him as he repeatedly steps into the road. On an island where everyone knows everyone, Officer Milton sends a photograph of the man to base, where his identity provides a surprising twist to the tale. It's a race against time for Officer Milton to get him returned home safely.
Elsewhere, PC Eddie Smith and PC Jameela Sabir are on a stop-and-search operation. When Sergeant Mervin Homer examines a bike, he discovers a dangerous switchblade hidden under the seat. With the rider offering no feasible explanation, the prohibited weapon is immediately seized. Back at Hamilton Police Station, Custody Sergeant Francis Blackman reads the bike rider their rights, while Assistant Commissioner Martin Weekes examines other recently confiscated blades, including machetes and a samurai sword.
At Bermuda’s international airport, PC Paul 'Geordie' Watson supports Customs Officer Malcolm Martin and drugs dog Zorro while screening an incoming flight from Canada. After sweeping the aircraft cabin in just five minutes, Zorro indicates interest in two bags in the arrivals hall, leaving customs officers the job of discreetly monitoring the family before searching their bags and bringing them in for questioning. What will the canine team uncover next?

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
Claire McCollum is in Glasgow to celebrate Advent Sunday, a special time of waiting for Christ’s arrival, and St Andrew’s Day to see how Scotland’s patron saint continues to inspire Christians today.
At the magnificent St Andrew’s Cathedral, Claire explores the story of Scotland’s patron saint with theologian and Quaker Alastair McIntosh. Originally a fisherman, Andrew was among the first disciples called by Jesus and went on to dedicate his life to spreading Christ’s message.
Today, that same spirit of Christian faith and service can be seen at Glasgow City Mission, a Christian charity that has supported people on the margins of society for 200 years, offering rehabilitation support, creative classes and hot meals.
Among those making a difference is support worker Angela Wilson, who first came to the charity for help 25 years ago. As Claire discovers more about the mission’s work, she meets some of its guests, visits its art class and choir, and hears how the charity has transformed lives. Together, they explore how the mission seeks to embody the Advent themes of hope, peace, joy and love.
The story comes full circle at Troon Harbour, where the Fishermen’s Mission continues St Andrew’s legacy of supporting those who make their living at sea. Area officer Louise Liddell explains how the organisation offers practical, financial and faith-based support to fishermen and their families throughout their lives.
With music to celebrate Advent Sunday and St Andrew’s Day, including a new recording from Celtic Worship.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
In the frozen waters of the Arctic, a bowhead whale breaks the sea ice with its skull to breathe - completely at home in this seemingly hostile sea. Polar waters may seem remote, but their influence supports more than the wildlife that thrives there by helping to power a global system of ocean currents that creates extraordinary opportunities for wildlife far beyond the ice.
In the Falkland Islands, nutrient-rich water flowing north from Antarctica sustains a colony of king penguins. But returning parents weighed down with food for their chicks must try to cross a beach patrolled by an extraordinary southern sea lion, the only one known to regularly hunt king penguins on land.
Cold water from the Arctic also travels thousands of miles. In the Pacific, it cools the coast of Japan, where a male dwarf lumpsucker, about the size of a pea, must find a nest and persuade a female to enter. Once she has laid her eggs, he becomes a devoted single father, guarding them from hungry predators for 40 days and nights.
Around Antarctica, hundreds of fin whales converge on one of the greatest feeding grounds on earth. They work together in a spectacular synchronised formation, turning clockwise before lunging onto their sides to feast on Antarctic krill. Beneath the continent’s sea ice lies a remarkable world where giant sea spiders clamber over ancient glass sponges and a tiny amphipod escapes hungry icefish by hitching a ride on sea angels and venomous jellyfish.
The influence of the polar waters is so strong that it helps power global currents that cross entire oceans and circle the planet. In the North Atlantic, the Gulf Stream brings warm water from the Caribbean to the shores of Britain, attracting Atlantic bluefin tuna to hunt off the Cornish coast. These powerful predators, which can attack at 45 miles per hour, have only recently returned to British shores following international action to protect them.
But the currents all these animals rely on are changing. With a loss of sea ice, many are now weakening, driving animals to adapt – sometimes in surprising ways. Around Newfoundland, green sea urchins are losing the kelp forests that once protected them from the sun’s ultraviolet rays.

programme.sub-title: Swanage Pier and Seafront, Dorset 3 ║ S46
programme.desc:
The roadshow pays a final visit to Swanage Pier in Dorset, where treasures include shipwreck finds, a jewel-encrusted bird, an early folding bike and a pair of aviator boots with a link to a tragic wartime mission.
Ronnie Archer-Morgan is moved by a powerful sculpture from South Africa, while Serhat Ahmet celebrates trailblazing potter Hannah Barlow when he sees a rare example of her artistry in ceramics. Siobhan Tyrrell sees items of motoring memorabilia that belonged to pioneering female driver Ivy Cummings, while Geoffrey Munn is dazzled by a jewel-encrusted brooch in the shape of a mysterious bird.
Mark Hill admires the engineering that has gone into a homemade folding bike, while Mark Smith is moved to tears by a pair of aviator’s boots that have a link to a tragic wartime mission that involved his late father. Marc Allum meets members of a local diving group and is intrigued to see a collection of First World War keepsakes salvaged from the wreck of the Kyrra, sunk by a German U-boat in May 1918, while Justin Croft sees a thrilling first-hand survivor’s account of a much earlier shipwreck.
Fiona finds out about the history of the Swanage lifeboat and the wider history of the RNLI, which is marking its bicentenary, and tries to put three ancient fossils in order of age in a quirky geological challenge set by Marc Allum. programme.title: Heal with the Princess of Wales
programme.desc:
Introduced by Kirsty Young
Acquired for the BBC, the Princess’s deeply personal film explores life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.
It follows the Princess on a journey through some of Britain's most spectacular landscapes as she undertakes the National Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales, to meet her family at the finish line.
Set against the backdrop of the challenge itself, the Princess reflects on her own experience alongside individuals navigating their own health journeys. Together, they explore the profound impact serious illness can have on the whole person, and the people, places and experiences that can help us heal.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
A journey into the last great frontier on earth. Beneath the ocean's surface lies a vast, largely unknown realm of deep coral reefs, towering mountains, volcanoes and hydrothermal vents, all part of the largest living space on the planet. Once thought to be empty and inaccessible, this hidden world is now yielding its secrets. New technology, including remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), is taking us further into this realm than ever before, revealing an astonishing abundance of life and some of the most exciting discoveries of our time.
In the Pacific, a young female argonaut, no bigger than a garden pea, joins the greatest movement of life on earth. Every night, trillions of animals rise from the depths to feed near the surface. Unable to travel such immense distances alone, they have evolved an ingenious solution: hitchhiking aboard other animals as they journey through the open ocean.
As sunlight fades, the animals of the deep create light of their own - bioluminescence. A flash can lure prey, provide camouflage, warn an attacker or carry a message through the darkness. Yet much of this ancient language of living light remains a mystery.
Deeper still, beneath immense pressure and suspended in an apparently boundless expanse, life takes on extraordinary forms. Siphonophores drift through the darkness. Each may appear to be a single animal, but it is in fact an entire colony of specialised individuals working together. Some have remarkable body forms, including one which scientists describe as the ‘flying spaghetti monster’. Laser imaging systems are allowing scientists to study these extraordinarily delicate creatures, revealing their hidden lives in spectacular ways and discovering new species in the process.
On the seabed, seemingly endless plains give way to extraordinary worlds - if you follow the clues to find them. Methane escaping from deep beneath the sea floor creates oases of life in the Arctic. Forests of corals flourish in perpetual darkness, providing food and shelter for countless animals, with some colonies having survived for thousands of years. On a volcanic seamount off Canada, more than two million skate eggs blanket the summit, forming the largest deep sea nursery yet discovered.

programme.title: Amanda & Alan's Spanish Job
programme.desc:
Best friends Amanda and Alan return to Spain in the festive season for a one-off Christmas special. They’re back in the village of Moclin, where they spent a long, hot summer turning an old wreck into a dreamy B&B. Before they put the house on the market, they want to throw one final party to say thank you to all their friends who helped them with the project.
Reuniting with some old faces, Amanda and Alan reveal that they want to celebrate an Anglo-Spanish Christmas, which will culminate in them hosting a big feast at their Moclin home. Keen to learn what local festive traditions they can adopt, Alan suspects it will be a unique experience, while Amanda warns there will be a couple of their own British traditions thrown in for good measure.
After Alan professes a love of Christmas maximalism, Amanda worries that his festive decorating skills could be up there with his actual decorating skills. Not wanting anything clumsy this season, Amanda is all about a classy Christmas aesthetic when it comes to decorating their house. Unfortunately, Alan has other ideas as he heads to buy some tree decorations and gets carried away in the tinsel department.
With a menu to plan, the two friends swap their boiler suits for aprons. Alan invites over his favourite local, Marco the mayor, to help prepare his mum’s shrimp cocktail. But the mayor’s penchant for Tabasco nearly upends Alan’s precious recipe, and he has a job on his hands to keep his sous chef under control!
Meanwhile, Amanda is in charge of desserts and visits one of Granada’s oldest bakeries to learn about Spain’s famous three kings cake, where gifts are hidden and the finder of the king is rewarded with special treatment for the day. Not to be outdone by Spanish traditions, Amanda introduces the locals to her nan’s famous sherry trifle. Who better to help her than her favourite sherry man, Juan, who travels over from Jerez to assist? The two of them embrace the festive spirit, and their dinner guests are in for a treat as Amanda is especially liberal with the quantity of sherry mixed into the cream.
Away from the menu planning, the two best friends make the most of the Christmas season to enjoy other Andalusian delights.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.sub-title: Dundee - A Repair for a Scottish Football Legend ║ S1
programme.desc:
In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero.
Dom and Lucia are in Dundee, where regeneration of the waterfront has sparked change throughout the city. However, in the shadow of the celebrated RSS Discovery, Scotland’s oldest wooden ship, HMS Unicorn, is moored around the corner and a little neglected. Beloved by many, especially the generations of the Women's Royal Naval Service who trained on it, the 200-year-old vessel is in need of immediate preservation. However, getting it into dry dock is a costly operation, so the team are visiting to help with the fundraising efforts. In the past, a fibreglass copy of the unicorn figurehead went on tour to raise awareness of the project, but it has been unable to perform those duties since it was damaged a decade ago. Despite some recent health troubles, heraldic sculptor Peter is eager to repair the figurehead so that it can go out on its fundraising excursions once again.
It’s all to play for when Dom picks up a Scotland Schoolboys football cap that holds immense significance for Amanda. It was awarded to her husband Frank, who became a legend at local club Dundee United, playing there for a decade. But after retirement, Frank suffered from vascular dementia, and he would cradle the cap often, serving as a reminder of earlier days. Now, the gold brocade is tarnished, and the navy blue fabric faded, so master hatter Jayesh Vaghela has his work cut out to restore it to how it looked when Frank first held it all those years ago.
Lucia trained at the V&A in London, but this is her chance to visit the Dundee branch of the celebrated art and design museum. She is there to learn about their restoration of a lost Charles Rennie Mackintosh-designed interior. Originally in Miss Cranston’s Ingram Street Tearooms in Glasgow, the interior was painstakingly moved and rebuilt in Dundee. Bringing a work like this out of storage and back to the public is a conservator’s dream, and Lucia can’t wait to hear all about it.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
The second group of five professional chefs step out of the MasterChef kitchen and into the competitive world of pop-up dining.
Birmingham’s vibrant Saint Paul’s Market plays host to the MasterChef: The Professionals pop-up, where the five chefs must impress 25 specially invited diners and pop-up industry experts with a dish that could have customers queuing around the block.
Bold flavours, originality and the ability to deliver food that works on a busy service are essential. Marcus and Monica are on hand to offer encouragement and sample the dishes, but the ultimate decision rests with the diners, who vote for their favourite. For one chef, their verdict means a straight passage into the semi-finals.
For those who miss out on that coveted place, there is one final chance to prove they belong in the competition. This time, the challenge is fish offal, an ingredient that demands real culinary knowledge and ingenuity. With sustainability an increasingly important part of professional cooking, making use of the whole fish is a valuable skill, reduces waste and unlocks a wealth of flavours and textures. The chefs must turn these often overlooked ingredients into a sophisticated, restaurant-worthy dish that showcases both their technical skill and creative flair. With time against them and a semi-final place on the line, there is no room for caution or error.
The three chefs who impress Marcus and Monica the most join the winner of the pop-up challenge, completing the line-up of eight semi-finalists. For one chef, however, their MasterChef journey comes to an end.
The competition is reaching its defining stages, and the race to become MasterChef: The Professionals Champion 2026 is well and truly on. programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc:
Antiques meet archaeology in this episode from West Sussex. In the village of Fishbourne, Natasha Raskin Sharp learns about the discovery of a huge Roman palace by workmen in the 1960s. In the company of curator Dr Rob Symmons, she hears how part of the palace and its treasures were unearthed over eight summers by hundreds of volunteers. One of the highlights is an exquisite mosaic featuring mythical sea creatures around which the owner – a high-ranking Roman – and his guests would have sat to eat meals. Another highlight is a partially smashed statue of Emperor Nero and a remarkably rare rabbit bone.
Hoping to unearth their own treasures are two teams of bargain hunters at Ardingly antiques fair. In blue are cousins Michelle and Emma, and in red are golfing pals Linda and Yvonne. With expert Caroline Hawley by their side, the reds get off to an explosive start, eyeing up a pair of powder flasks. Meanwhile, Emma spots a West German pottery vase, but expert Thomas Forrester doubts that profits will bloom at auction.
Wielding his gavel at the auction is Nick Hall; can the experts’ bonus buys bring home the big bucks? programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
When a burnt-out delivery van is discovered on a quiet rural road, Rose and Raj are met with a grim crime scene: a charred body in the passenger seat and no sign of the driver. Sifting through the ashes, they uncover a bizarre assortment of clues, including a melted key fob, rusted gardening tools and a bottle of imported Polish vodka.
Tracking down the van’s insured drivers leads them to Kelly Prudham, a tight-lipped agency cleaner, and Scott Smith, a devoted widowed father missing since the previous evening. Is Scott the vanished driver, or is he the unidentified victim in the passenger seat? Kelly claims concern for Scott’s young daughter Chloe, yet she stonewalls every question. However, Rose’s sharp eyes spot an identical bottle of Polish vodka in Kelly’s flat, indicating that Kelly may have a dangerous motive for concealing her and Scott’s recent movements.
Meanwhile, Joe can’t resist probing into the mystery. Dragging Brother Christopher along, he snoops around the crime scene and dives into Scott’s past. Relying on his sharp human intuition and feeling somewhat aligned with this man who seems to be struggling as a father, Joe forms a bold theory about Scott’s whereabouts. But his covert search goes sideways, stranding Joe and Christopher in a perilous predicament deep in the Northumbrian moors.
With time running out and danger escalating, Rose, Joe and Raj must pool their findings to identify the burnt remains, track down the arsonist and expose the motive behind the blaze before the truth burns out completely. programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.sub-title: East Lothian - Saving the Musselburgh Carriage ║ S1
programme.desc:
In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero.
Will and Kirsten are in Musselburgh, on Scotland’s east coast. It’s a town boasting a proud heritage that is celebrated each year with a procession led by their elected Honest Lad and Honest Lass. However, for the past few years, the antique carriage these local luminaries ride in has been off the road. Restoring the carriage is a huge job that requires the skills of local signwriter Ross Hastie and wheelwright Greg Rowland, and made more complicated by the impending deadline of this year’s festival.
It's a bit of a musical mystery when the team are faced with Erica’s Stroviol. In the family since the 1930s, it belonged to Erica's father, who was a passionate musician who played in several local groups. The distinctive horn has become detached from this turn-of-the-century musical oddity, so it might take more than just the skills of stringed instrument expert Becky Houghton to get a tune out of it once again.
In nearby Edinburgh, Will stops off at Stewart Christie & Co, Scotland’s oldest bespoke tailors, to discover how their handmade tweed clothes balance modern demands with century-old techniques. Will gets an insight into every step of the process, from an initial measuring to getting on the scissors himself and cutting out his own waistcoat pattern from the tweed cloth the company built their name on. programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc:
With exclusive access to the police service on the paradise island of Bermuda, we follow life on the front line for the near 400 officers keeping both holidaymakers and locals safe. From patrols and traffic operations to the drug unit, forensics, tactical response teams, the coastguard and community policing, the series goes behind the scenes with the officers at the heart of the action.
The island has its fair share of challenges on both land and sea, with more than 3,000 crimes committed each year. We show how these dedicated officers, including around 30 from the UK, deal with the highs and lows of policing this British Overseas Territory.
In the centre of the island, Sergeant Milton Hill responds to reports of an elderly man walking along a busy roadside in clear distress. When he arrives, the man is unable to recall his name, address or basic personal details, and the mystery begins. Concerned for his safety, Milton stays close, guiding traffic around him as he repeatedly steps into the road. On an island where everyone knows everyone, Officer Milton sends a photograph of the man to base, where his identity provides a surprising twist to the tale. It's a race against time for Officer Milton to get him returned home safely.
Elsewhere, PC Eddie Smith and PC Jameela Sabir are on a stop-and-search operation. When Sergeant Mervin Homer examines a bike, he discovers a dangerous switchblade hidden under the seat. With the rider offering no feasible explanation, the prohibited weapon is immediately seized. Back at Hamilton Police Station, Custody Sergeant Francis Blackman reads the bike rider their rights, while Assistant Commissioner Martin Weekes examines other recently confiscated blades, including machetes and a samurai sword.
At Bermuda’s international airport, PC Paul 'Geordie' Watson supports Customs Officer Malcolm Martin and drugs dog Zorro while screening an incoming flight from Canada. After sweeping the aircraft cabin in just five minutes, Zorro indicates interest in two bags in the arrivals hall, leaving customs officers the job of discreetly monitoring the family before searching their bags and bringing them in for questioning. What will the canine team uncover next?

Mackenzie has her work cut out, with decades separating the investigation from the crime. The grim discovery stirs painful memories of Philomena's past, forcing her to confront history and heartache. Glenn's no stranger to that as he struggles to let go of his feelings for Mack, all while her connection with his replacement Leo blooms. programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
Claire McCollum is in Glasgow to celebrate Advent Sunday, a special time of waiting for Christ’s arrival, and St Andrew’s Day to see how Scotland’s patron saint continues to inspire Christians today.
At the magnificent St Andrew’s Cathedral, Claire explores the story of Scotland’s patron saint with theologian and Quaker Alastair McIntosh. Originally a fisherman, Andrew was among the first disciples called by Jesus and went on to dedicate his life to spreading Christ’s message.
Today, that same spirit of Christian faith and service can be seen at Glasgow City Mission, a Christian charity that has supported people on the margins of society for 200 years, offering rehabilitation support, creative classes and hot meals.
Among those making a difference is support worker Angela Wilson, who first came to the charity for help 25 years ago. As Claire discovers more about the mission’s work, she meets some of its guests, visits its art class and choir, and hears how the charity has transformed lives. Together, they explore how the mission seeks to embody the Advent themes of hope, peace, joy and love.
The story comes full circle at Troon Harbour, where the Fishermen’s Mission continues St Andrew’s legacy of supporting those who make their living at sea. Area officer Louise Liddell explains how the organisation offers practical, financial and faith-based support to fishermen and their families throughout their lives.
With music to celebrate Advent Sunday and St Andrew’s Day, including a new recording from Celtic Worship.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
In the frozen waters of the Arctic, a bowhead whale breaks the sea ice with its skull to breathe - completely at home in this seemingly hostile sea. Polar waters may seem remote, but their influence supports more than the wildlife that thrives there by helping to power a global system of ocean currents that creates extraordinary opportunities for wildlife far beyond the ice.
In the Falkland Islands, nutrient-rich water flowing north from Antarctica sustains a colony of king penguins. But returning parents weighed down with food for their chicks must try to cross a beach patrolled by an extraordinary southern sea lion, the only one known to regularly hunt king penguins on land.
Cold water from the Arctic also travels thousands of miles. In the Pacific, it cools the coast of Japan, where a male dwarf lumpsucker, about the size of a pea, must find a nest and persuade a female to enter. Once she has laid her eggs, he becomes a devoted single father, guarding them from hungry predators for 40 days and nights.
Around Antarctica, hundreds of fin whales converge on one of the greatest feeding grounds on earth. They work together in a spectacular synchronised formation, turning clockwise before lunging onto their sides to feast on Antarctic krill. Beneath the continent’s sea ice lies a remarkable world where giant sea spiders clamber over ancient glass sponges and a tiny amphipod escapes hungry icefish by hitching a ride on sea angels and venomous jellyfish.
The influence of the polar waters is so strong that it helps power global currents that cross entire oceans and circle the planet. In the North Atlantic, the Gulf Stream brings warm water from the Caribbean to the shores of Britain, attracting Atlantic bluefin tuna to hunt off the Cornish coast. These powerful predators, which can attack at 45 miles per hour, have only recently returned to British shores following international action to protect them.
But the currents all these animals rely on are changing. With a loss of sea ice, many are now weakening, driving animals to adapt – sometimes in surprising ways. Around Newfoundland, green sea urchins are losing the kelp forests that once protected them from the sun’s ultraviolet rays.

Margherita joins the volunteers preparing the lagoon’s nesting sites ahead of the spring breeding season, while Adam Henson is in Belfast for the BBC Food and Farming Awards to reveal Countryfile’s Young Countryside Champion 2026. programme.sub-title: Swanage Pier and Seafront, Dorset 3 ║ S46
programme.desc:
The roadshow pays a final visit to Swanage Pier in Dorset, where treasures include shipwreck finds, a jewel-encrusted bird, an early folding bike and a pair of aviator boots with a link to a tragic wartime mission.
Ronnie Archer-Morgan is moved by a powerful sculpture from South Africa, while Serhat Ahmet celebrates trailblazing potter Hannah Barlow when he sees a rare example of her artistry in ceramics. Siobhan Tyrrell sees items of motoring memorabilia that belonged to pioneering female driver Ivy Cummings, while Geoffrey Munn is dazzled by a jewel-encrusted brooch in the shape of a mysterious bird.
Mark Hill admires the engineering that has gone into a homemade folding bike, while Mark Smith is moved to tears by a pair of aviator’s boots that have a link to a tragic wartime mission that involved his late father. Marc Allum meets members of a local diving group and is intrigued to see a collection of First World War keepsakes salvaged from the wreck of the Kyrra, sunk by a German U-boat in May 1918, while Justin Croft sees a thrilling first-hand survivor’s account of a much earlier shipwreck.
Fiona finds out about the history of the Swanage lifeboat and the wider history of the RNLI, which is marking its bicentenary, and tries to put three ancient fossils in order of age in a quirky geological challenge set by Marc Allum. programme.title: Heal with the Princess of Wales
programme.desc:
Introduced by Kirsty Young
Acquired for the BBC, the Princess’s deeply personal film explores life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.
It follows the Princess on a journey through some of Britain's most spectacular landscapes as she undertakes the National Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales, to meet her family at the finish line.
Set against the backdrop of the challenge itself, the Princess reflects on her own experience alongside individuals navigating their own health journeys. Together, they explore the profound impact serious illness can have on the whole person, and the people, places and experiences that can help us heal.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
A journey into the last great frontier on earth. Beneath the ocean's surface lies a vast, largely unknown realm of deep coral reefs, towering mountains, volcanoes and hydrothermal vents, all part of the largest living space on the planet. Once thought to be empty and inaccessible, this hidden world is now yielding its secrets. New technology, including remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), is taking us further into this realm than ever before, revealing an astonishing abundance of life and some of the most exciting discoveries of our time.
In the Pacific, a young female argonaut, no bigger than a garden pea, joins the greatest movement of life on earth. Every night, trillions of animals rise from the depths to feed near the surface. Unable to travel such immense distances alone, they have evolved an ingenious solution: hitchhiking aboard other animals as they journey through the open ocean.
As sunlight fades, the animals of the deep create light of their own - bioluminescence. A flash can lure prey, provide camouflage, warn an attacker or carry a message through the darkness. Yet much of this ancient language of living light remains a mystery.
Deeper still, beneath immense pressure and suspended in an apparently boundless expanse, life takes on extraordinary forms. Siphonophores drift through the darkness. Each may appear to be a single animal, but it is in fact an entire colony of specialised individuals working together. Some have remarkable body forms, including one which scientists describe as the ‘flying spaghetti monster’. Laser imaging systems are allowing scientists to study these extraordinarily delicate creatures, revealing their hidden lives in spectacular ways and discovering new species in the process.
On the seabed, seemingly endless plains give way to extraordinary worlds - if you follow the clues to find them. Methane escaping from deep beneath the sea floor creates oases of life in the Arctic. Forests of corals flourish in perpetual darkness, providing food and shelter for countless animals, with some colonies having survived for thousands of years. On a volcanic seamount off Canada, more than two million skate eggs blanket the summit, forming the largest deep sea nursery yet discovered.

programme.title: Amanda & Alan's Spanish Job
programme.desc:
Best friends Amanda and Alan return to Spain in the festive season for a one-off Christmas special. They’re back in the village of Moclin, where they spent a long, hot summer turning an old wreck into a dreamy B&B. Before they put the house on the market, they want to throw one final party to say thank you to all their friends who helped them with the project.
Reuniting with some old faces, Amanda and Alan reveal that they want to celebrate an Anglo-Spanish Christmas, which will culminate in them hosting a big feast at their Moclin home. Keen to learn what local festive traditions they can adopt, Alan suspects it will be a unique experience, while Amanda warns there will be a couple of their own British traditions thrown in for good measure.
After Alan professes a love of Christmas maximalism, Amanda worries that his festive decorating skills could be up there with his actual decorating skills. Not wanting anything clumsy this season, Amanda is all about a classy Christmas aesthetic when it comes to decorating their house. Unfortunately, Alan has other ideas as he heads to buy some tree decorations and gets carried away in the tinsel department.
With a menu to plan, the two friends swap their boiler suits for aprons. Alan invites over his favourite local, Marco the mayor, to help prepare his mum’s shrimp cocktail. But the mayor’s penchant for Tabasco nearly upends Alan’s precious recipe, and he has a job on his hands to keep his sous chef under control!
Meanwhile, Amanda is in charge of desserts and visits one of Granada’s oldest bakeries to learn about Spain’s famous three kings cake, where gifts are hidden and the finder of the king is rewarded with special treatment for the day. Not to be outdone by Spanish traditions, Amanda introduces the locals to her nan’s famous sherry trifle. Who better to help her than her favourite sherry man, Juan, who travels over from Jerez to assist? The two of them embrace the festive spirit, and their dinner guests are in for a treat as Amanda is especially liberal with the quantity of sherry mixed into the cream.
Away from the menu planning, the two best friends make the most of the Christmas season to enjoy other Andalusian delights.
