programme.desc:
In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero.
Dom and Lucia are in Dundee, where regeneration of the waterfront has sparked change throughout the city. However, in the shadow of the celebrated RSS Discovery, Scotland’s oldest wooden ship, HMS Unicorn, is moored around the corner and a little neglected. Beloved by many, especially the generations of the Women's Royal Naval Service who trained on it, the 200-year-old vessel is in need of immediate preservation. However, getting it into dry dock is a costly operation, so the team are visiting to help with the fundraising efforts. In the past, a fibreglass copy of the unicorn figurehead went on tour to raise awareness of the project, but it has been unable to perform those duties since it was damaged a decade ago. Despite some recent health troubles, heraldic sculptor Peter is eager to repair the figurehead so that it can go out on its fundraising excursions once again.
It’s all to play for when Dom picks up a Scotland Schoolboys football cap that holds immense significance for Amanda. It was awarded to her husband Frank, who became a legend at local club Dundee United, playing there for a decade. But after retirement, Frank suffered from vascular dementia, and he would cradle the cap often, serving as a reminder of earlier days. Now, the gold brocade is tarnished, and the navy blue fabric faded, so master hatter Jayesh Vaghela has his work cut out to restore it to how it looked when Frank first held it all those years ago.
Lucia trained at the V&A in London, but this is her chance to visit the Dundee branch of the celebrated art and design museum. She is there to learn about their restoration of a lost Charles Rennie Mackintosh-designed interior. Originally in Miss Cranston’s Ingram Street Tearooms in Glasgow, the interior was painstakingly moved and rebuilt in Dundee. Bringing a work like this out of storage and back to the public is a conservator’s dream, and Lucia can’t wait to hear all about it.

The second group of five professional chefs step out of the MasterChef kitchen and into the competitive world of pop-up dining.
Birmingham’s vibrant Saint Paul’s Market plays host to the MasterChef: The Professionals pop-up, where the five chefs must impress 25 specially invited diners and pop-up industry experts with a dish that could have customers queuing around the block.

Marcus and Monica are on hand to offer encouragement and sample the dishes, but the ultimate decision rests with the diners, who vote for their favourite. For one chef, their verdict means a straight passage into the semi-finals.
For those who miss out on that coveted place, there is one final chance to prove they belong in the competition. This time, the challenge is fish offal, an ingredient that demands real culinary knowledge and ingenuity. With sustainability an increasingly important part of professional cooking, making use of the whole fish is a valuable skill, reduces waste and unlocks a wealth of flavours and textures. The chefs must turn these often overlooked ingredients into a sophisticated, restaurant-worthy dish that showcases both their technical skill and creative flair. With time against them and a semi-final place on the line, there is no room for caution or error.
The three chefs who impress Marcus and Monica the most join the winner of the pop-up challenge, completing the line-up of eight semi-finalists. For one chef, however, their MasterChef journey comes to an end.
The competition is reaching its defining stages, and the race to become MasterChef: The Professionals Champion 2026 is well and truly on. programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
When a burnt-out delivery van is discovered on a quiet rural road, Rose and Raj are met with a grim crime scene: a charred body in the passenger seat and no sign of the driver. Sifting through the ashes, they uncover a bizarre assortment of clues, including a melted key fob, rusted gardening tools and a bottle of imported Polish vodka.
Tracking down the van’s insured drivers leads them to Kelly Prudham, a tight-lipped agency cleaner, and Scott Smith, a devoted widowed father missing since the previous evening. Is Scott the vanished driver, or is he the unidentified victim in the passenger seat? Kelly claims concern for Scott’s young daughter Chloe, yet she stonewalls every question. However, Rose’s sharp eyes spot an identical bottle of Polish vodka in Kelly’s flat, indicating that Kelly may have a dangerous motive for concealing her and Scott’s recent movements.
Meanwhile, Joe can’t resist probing into the mystery. Dragging Brother Christopher along, he snoops around the crime scene and dives into Scott’s past. Relying on his sharp human intuition and feeling somewhat aligned with this man who seems to be struggling as a father, Joe forms a bold theory about Scott’s whereabouts. But his covert search goes sideways, stranding Joe and Christopher in a perilous predicament deep in the Northumbrian moors.
With time running out and danger escalating, Rose, Joe and Raj must pool their findings to identify the burnt remains, track down the arsonist and expose the motive behind the blaze before the truth burns out completely. Restoring the carriage is a huge job that requires the skills of local signwriter Ross Hastie and wheelwright Greg Rowland, and made more complicated by the impending deadline of this year’s festival.
It's a bit of a musical mystery when the team are faced with Erica’s Stroviol. In the family since the 1930s, it belonged to Erica's father, who was a passionate musician who played in several local groups. The distinctive horn has become detached from this turn-of-the-century musical oddity, so it might take more than just the skills of stringed instrument expert Becky Houghton to get a tune out of it once again.
In nearby Edinburgh, Will stops off at Stewart Christie & Co, Scotland’s oldest bespoke tailors, to discover how their handmade tweed clothes balance modern demands with century-old techniques. Will gets an insight into every step of the process, from an initial measuring to getting on the scissors himself and cutting out his own waistcoat pattern from the tweed cloth the company built their name on. programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc:
With exclusive access to the police service on the paradise island of Bermuda, we follow life on the front line for the near 400 officers keeping both holidaymakers and locals safe. From patrols and traffic operations to the drug unit, forensics, tactical response teams, the coastguard and community policing, the series goes behind the scenes with the officers at the heart of the action.
The island has its fair share of challenges on both land and sea, with more than 3,000 crimes committed each year. We show how these dedicated officers, including around 30 from the UK, deal with the highs and lows of policing this British Overseas Territory.
In the centre of the island, Sergeant Milton Hill responds to reports of an elderly man walking along a busy roadside in clear distress. When he arrives, the man is unable to recall his name, address or basic personal details, and the mystery begins. Concerned for his safety, Milton stays close, guiding traffic around him as he repeatedly steps into the road. On an island where everyone knows everyone, Officer Milton sends a photograph of the man to base, where his identity provides a surprising twist to the tale. It's a race against time for Officer Milton to get him returned home safely.
Elsewhere, PC Eddie Smith and PC Jameela Sabir are on a stop-and-search operation. When Sergeant Mervin Homer examines a bike, he discovers a dangerous switchblade hidden under the seat. With the rider offering no feasible explanation, the prohibited weapon is immediately seized. Back at Hamilton Police Station, Custody Sergeant Francis Blackman reads the bike rider their rights, while Assistant Commissioner Martin Weekes examines other recently confiscated blades, including machetes and a samurai sword.
At Bermuda’s international airport, PC Paul 'Geordie' Watson supports Customs Officer Malcolm Martin and drugs dog Zorro while screening an incoming flight from Canada. After sweeping the aircraft cabin in just five minutes, Zorro indicates interest in two bags in the arrivals hall, leaving customs officers the job of discreetly monitoring the family before searching their bags and bringing them in for questioning. What will the canine team uncover next?

Mackenzie has her work cut out, with decades separating the investigation from the crime. The grim discovery stirs painful memories of Philomena's past, forcing her to confront history and heartache. Glenn's no stranger to that as he struggles to let go of his feelings for Mack, all while her connection with his replacement Leo blooms. programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
Claire McCollum is in Glasgow to celebrate Advent Sunday, a special time of waiting for Christ’s arrival, and St Andrew’s Day to see how Scotland’s patron saint continues to inspire Christians today.
At the magnificent St Andrew’s Cathedral, Claire explores the story of Scotland’s patron saint with theologian and Quaker Alastair McIntosh. Originally a fisherman, Andrew was among the first disciples called by Jesus and went on to dedicate his life to spreading Christ’s message.
Today, that same spirit of Christian faith and service can be seen at Glasgow City Mission, a Christian charity that has supported people on the margins of society for 200 years, offering rehabilitation support, creative classes and hot meals.
Among those making a difference is support worker Angela Wilson, who first came to the charity for help 25 years ago. As Claire discovers more about the mission’s work, she meets some of its guests, visits its art class and choir, and hears how the charity has transformed lives. Together, they explore how the mission seeks to embody the Advent themes of hope, peace, joy and love.
The story comes full circle at Troon Harbour, where the Fishermen’s Mission continues St Andrew’s legacy of supporting those who make their living at sea. Area officer Louise Liddell explains how the organisation offers practical, financial and faith-based support to fishermen and their families throughout their lives.
With music to celebrate Advent Sunday and St Andrew’s Day, including a new recording from Celtic Worship.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
In the frozen waters of the Arctic, a bowhead whale breaks the sea ice with its skull to breathe - completely at home in this seemingly hostile sea. Polar waters may seem remote, but their influence supports more than the wildlife that thrives there by helping to power a global system of ocean currents that creates extraordinary opportunities for wildlife far beyond the ice.
In the Falkland Islands, nutrient-rich water flowing north from Antarctica sustains a colony of king penguins. But returning parents weighed down with food for their chicks must try to cross a beach patrolled by an extraordinary southern sea lion, the only one known to regularly hunt king penguins on land.
Cold water from the Arctic also travels thousands of miles. In the Pacific, it cools the coast of Japan, where a male dwarf lumpsucker, about the size of a pea, must find a nest and persuade a female to enter. Once she has laid her eggs, he becomes a devoted single father, guarding them from hungry predators for 40 days and nights.
Around Antarctica, hundreds of fin whales converge on one of the greatest feeding grounds on earth. They work together in a spectacular synchronised formation, turning clockwise before lunging onto their sides to feast on Antarctic krill. Beneath the continent’s sea ice lies a remarkable world where giant sea spiders clamber over ancient glass sponges and a tiny amphipod escapes hungry icefish by hitching a ride on sea angels and venomous jellyfish.
The influence of the polar waters is so strong that it helps power global currents that cross entire oceans and circle the planet. In the North Atlantic, the Gulf Stream brings warm water from the Caribbean to the shores of Britain, attracting Atlantic bluefin tuna to hunt off the Cornish coast. These powerful predators, which can attack at 45 miles per hour, have only recently returned to British shores following international action to protect them.
But the currents all these animals rely on are changing. With a loss of sea ice, many are now weakening, driving animals to adapt – sometimes in surprising ways. Around Newfoundland, green sea urchins are losing the kelp forests that once protected them from the sun’s ultraviolet rays.

Matt Baker and Margherita Taylor visit RSPB Freiston Shore in Lincolnshire to see an ambitious engineering project being unveiled - a saline lagoon created to provide an ecologically important habitat alongside the Wash.

Margherita joins the volunteers preparing the lagoon’s nesting sites ahead of the spring breeding season, while Adam Henson is in Belfast for the BBC Food and Farming Awards to reveal Countryfile’s Young Countryside Champion 2026. programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.sub-title: Swanage Pier and Seafront, Dorset 3 ║ S46
programme.desc:
The roadshow pays a final visit to Swanage Pier in Dorset, where treasures include shipwreck finds, a jewel-encrusted bird, an early folding bike and a pair of aviator boots with a link to a tragic wartime mission.
Ronnie Archer-Morgan is moved by a powerful sculpture from South Africa, while Serhat Ahmet celebrates trailblazing potter Hannah Barlow when he sees a rare example of her artistry in ceramics. Siobhan Tyrrell sees items of motoring memorabilia that belonged to pioneering female driver Ivy Cummings, while Geoffrey Munn is dazzled by a jewel-encrusted brooch in the shape of a mysterious bird.
Mark Hill admires the engineering that has gone into a homemade folding bike, while Mark Smith is moved to tears by a pair of aviator’s boots that have a link to a tragic wartime mission that involved his late father. Marc Allum meets members of a local diving group and is intrigued to see a collection of First World War keepsakes salvaged from the wreck of the Kyrra, sunk by a German U-boat in May 1918, while Justin Croft sees a thrilling first-hand survivor’s account of a much earlier shipwreck.
Fiona finds out about the history of the Swanage lifeboat and the wider history of the RNLI, which is marking its bicentenary, and tries to put three ancient fossils in order of age in a quirky geological challenge set by Marc Allum. programme.title: Heal with the Princess of Wales
programme.desc:
Introduced by Kirsty Young
Acquired for the BBC, the Princess’s deeply personal film explores life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.
It follows the Princess on a journey through some of Britain's most spectacular landscapes as she undertakes the National Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales, to meet her family at the finish line.
Set against the backdrop of the challenge itself, the Princess reflects on her own experience alongside individuals navigating their own health journeys. Together, they explore the profound impact serious illness can have on the whole person, and the people, places and experiences that can help us heal.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
A journey into the last great frontier on earth. Beneath the ocean's surface lies a vast, largely unknown realm of deep coral reefs, towering mountains, volcanoes and hydrothermal vents, all part of the largest living space on the planet. Once thought to be empty and inaccessible, this hidden world is now yielding its secrets. New technology, including remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), is taking us further into this realm than ever before, revealing an astonishing abundance of life and some of the most exciting discoveries of our time.
In the Pacific, a young female argonaut, no bigger than a garden pea, joins the greatest movement of life on earth. Every night, trillions of animals rise from the depths to feed near the surface. Unable to travel such immense distances alone, they have evolved an ingenious solution: hitchhiking aboard other animals as they journey through the open ocean.
As sunlight fades, the animals of the deep create light of their own - bioluminescence. A flash can lure prey, provide camouflage, warn an attacker or carry a message through the darkness. Yet much of this ancient language of living light remains a mystery.
Deeper still, beneath immense pressure and suspended in an apparently boundless expanse, life takes on extraordinary forms. Siphonophores drift through the darkness. Each may appear to be a single animal, but it is in fact an entire colony of specialised individuals working together. Some have remarkable body forms, including one which scientists describe as the ‘flying spaghetti monster’. Laser imaging systems are allowing scientists to study these extraordinarily delicate creatures, revealing their hidden lives in spectacular ways and discovering new species in the process.
On the seabed, seemingly endless plains give way to extraordinary worlds - if you follow the clues to find them. Methane escaping from deep beneath the sea floor creates oases of life in the Arctic. Forests of corals flourish in perpetual darkness, providing food and shelter for countless animals, with some colonies having survived for thousands of years. On a volcanic seamount off Canada, more than two million skate eggs blanket the summit, forming the largest deep sea nursery yet discovered.

After Alan professes a love of Christmas maximalism, Amanda worries that his festive decorating skills could be up there with his actual decorating skills. Not wanting anything clumsy this season, Amanda is all about a classy Christmas aesthetic when it comes to decorating their house. Unfortunately, Alan has other ideas as he heads to buy some tree decorations and gets carried away in the tinsel department.
With a menu to plan, the two friends swap their boiler suits for aprons. Alan invites over his favourite local, Marco the mayor, to help prepare his mum’s shrimp cocktail. But the mayor’s penchant for Tabasco nearly upends Alan’s precious recipe, and he has a job on his hands to keep his sous chef under control!
Meanwhile, Amanda is in charge of desserts and visits one of Granada’s oldest bakeries to learn about Spain’s famous three kings cake, where gifts are hidden and the finder of the king is rewarded with special treatment for the day. Not to be outdone by Spanish traditions, Amanda introduces the locals to her nan’s famous sherry trifle. Who better to help her than her favourite sherry man, Juan, who travels over from Jerez to assist? The two of them embrace the festive spirit, and their dinner guests are in for a treat as Amanda is especially liberal with the quantity of sherry mixed into the cream.
Away from the menu planning, the two best friends make the most of the Christmas season to enjoy other Andalusian delights.

programme.sub-title: Dundee - A Repair for a Scottish Football Legend ║ S1
programme.desc:
In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero.
Dom and Lucia are in Dundee, where regeneration of the waterfront has sparked change throughout the city. However, in the shadow of the celebrated RSS Discovery, Scotland’s oldest wooden ship, HMS Unicorn, is moored around the corner and a little neglected. Beloved by many, especially the generations of the Women's Royal Naval Service who trained on it, the 200-year-old vessel is in need of immediate preservation. However, getting it into dry dock is a costly operation, so the team are visiting to help with the fundraising efforts. In the past, a fibreglass copy of the unicorn figurehead went on tour to raise awareness of the project, but it has been unable to perform those duties since it was damaged a decade ago. Despite some recent health troubles, heraldic sculptor Peter is eager to repair the figurehead so that it can go out on its fundraising excursions once again.
It’s all to play for when Dom picks up a Scotland Schoolboys football cap that holds immense significance for Amanda. It was awarded to her husband Frank, who became a legend at local club Dundee United, playing there for a decade. But after retirement, Frank suffered from vascular dementia, and he would cradle the cap often, serving as a reminder of earlier days. Now, the gold brocade is tarnished, and the navy blue fabric faded, so master hatter Jayesh Vaghela has his work cut out to restore it to how it looked when Frank first held it all those years ago.
Lucia trained at the V&A in London, but this is her chance to visit the Dundee branch of the celebrated art and design museum. She is there to learn about their restoration of a lost Charles Rennie Mackintosh-designed interior. Originally in Miss Cranston’s Ingram Street Tearooms in Glasgow, the interior was painstakingly moved and rebuilt in Dundee. Bringing a work like this out of storage and back to the public is a conservator’s dream, and Lucia can’t wait to hear all about it.

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
Claire McCollum is in Glasgow to celebrate Advent Sunday, a special time of waiting for Christ’s arrival, and St Andrew’s Day to see how Scotland’s patron saint continues to inspire Christians today.
At the magnificent St Andrew’s Cathedral, Claire explores the story of Scotland’s patron saint with theologian and Quaker Alastair McIntosh. Originally a fisherman, Andrew was among the first disciples called by Jesus and went on to dedicate his life to spreading Christ’s message.
Today, that same spirit of Christian faith and service can be seen at Glasgow City Mission, a Christian charity that has supported people on the margins of society for 200 years, offering rehabilitation support, creative classes and hot meals.
Among those making a difference is support worker Angela Wilson, who first came to the charity for help 25 years ago. As Claire discovers more about the mission’s work, she meets some of its guests, visits its art class and choir, and hears how the charity has transformed lives. Together, they explore how the mission seeks to embody the Advent themes of hope, peace, joy and love.
The story comes full circle at Troon Harbour, where the Fishermen’s Mission continues St Andrew’s legacy of supporting those who make their living at sea. Area officer Louise Liddell explains how the organisation offers practical, financial and faith-based support to fishermen and their families throughout their lives.
With music to celebrate Advent Sunday and St Andrew’s Day, including a new recording from Celtic Worship.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
In the frozen waters of the Arctic, a bowhead whale breaks the sea ice with its skull to breathe - completely at home in this seemingly hostile sea. Polar waters may seem remote, but their influence supports more than the wildlife that thrives there by helping to power a global system of ocean currents that creates extraordinary opportunities for wildlife far beyond the ice.
In the Falkland Islands, nutrient-rich water flowing north from Antarctica sustains a colony of king penguins. But returning parents weighed down with food for their chicks must try to cross a beach patrolled by an extraordinary southern sea lion, the only one known to regularly hunt king penguins on land.
Cold water from the Arctic also travels thousands of miles. In the Pacific, it cools the coast of Japan, where a male dwarf lumpsucker, about the size of a pea, must find a nest and persuade a female to enter. Once she has laid her eggs, he becomes a devoted single father, guarding them from hungry predators for 40 days and nights.
Around Antarctica, hundreds of fin whales converge on one of the greatest feeding grounds on earth. They work together in a spectacular synchronised formation, turning clockwise before lunging onto their sides to feast on Antarctic krill. Beneath the continent’s sea ice lies a remarkable world where giant sea spiders clamber over ancient glass sponges and a tiny amphipod escapes hungry icefish by hitching a ride on sea angels and venomous jellyfish.
The influence of the polar waters is so strong that it helps power global currents that cross entire oceans and circle the planet. In the North Atlantic, the Gulf Stream brings warm water from the Caribbean to the shores of Britain, attracting Atlantic bluefin tuna to hunt off the Cornish coast. These powerful predators, which can attack at 45 miles per hour, have only recently returned to British shores following international action to protect them.
But the currents all these animals rely on are changing. With a loss of sea ice, many are now weakening, driving animals to adapt – sometimes in surprising ways. Around Newfoundland, green sea urchins are losing the kelp forests that once protected them from the sun’s ultraviolet rays.

programme.desc:

Ronnie Archer-Morgan is moved by a powerful sculpture from South Africa, while Serhat Ahmet celebrates trailblazing potter Hannah Barlow when he sees a rare example of her artistry in ceramics. Mark Hill admires the engineering that has gone into a homemade folding bike, while Mark Smith is moved to tears by a pair of aviator’s boots that have a link to a tragic wartime mission that involved his late father. Marc Allum meets members of a local diving group and is intrigued to see a collection of First World War keepsakes salvaged from the wreck of the Kyrra, sunk by a German U-boat in May 1918, while Justin Croft sees a thrilling first-hand survivor’s account of a much earlier shipwreck.

programme.title: Heal with the Princess of Wales
programme.desc:
Introduced by Kirsty Young
Acquired for the BBC, the Princess’s deeply personal film explores life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.
It follows the Princess on a journey through some of Britain's most spectacular landscapes as she undertakes the National Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales, to meet her family at the finish line.
Set against the backdrop of the challenge itself, the Princess reflects on her own experience alongside individuals navigating their own health journeys. Together, they explore the profound impact serious illness can have on the whole person, and the people, places and experiences that can help us heal.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
A journey into the last great frontier on earth. Beneath the ocean's surface lies a vast, largely unknown realm of deep coral reefs, towering mountains, volcanoes and hydrothermal vents, all part of the largest living space on the planet. Once thought to be empty and inaccessible, this hidden world is now yielding its secrets. New technology, including remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), is taking us further into this realm than ever before, revealing an astonishing abundance of life and some of the most exciting discoveries of our time.
In the Pacific, a young female argonaut, no bigger than a garden pea, joins the greatest movement of life on earth. Every night, trillions of animals rise from the depths to feed near the surface. Unable to travel such immense distances alone, they have evolved an ingenious solution: hitchhiking aboard other animals as they journey through the open ocean.
As sunlight fades, the animals of the deep create light of their own - bioluminescence. A flash can lure prey, provide camouflage, warn an attacker or carry a message through the darkness. Yet much of this ancient language of living light remains a mystery.
Deeper still, beneath immense pressure and suspended in an apparently boundless expanse, life takes on extraordinary forms. Siphonophores drift through the darkness. Each may appear to be a single animal, but it is in fact an entire colony of specialised individuals working together. Some have remarkable body forms, including one which scientists describe as the ‘flying spaghetti monster’. Laser imaging systems are allowing scientists to study these extraordinarily delicate creatures, revealing their hidden lives in spectacular ways and discovering new species in the process.
On the seabed, seemingly endless plains give way to extraordinary worlds - if you follow the clues to find them. Methane escaping from deep beneath the sea floor creates oases of life in the Arctic. Forests of corals flourish in perpetual darkness, providing food and shelter for countless animals, with some colonies having survived for thousands of years. On a volcanic seamount off Canada, more than two million skate eggs blanket the summit, forming the largest deep sea nursery yet discovered.

programme.title: Amanda & Alan's Spanish Job
programme.desc:
Best friends Amanda and Alan return to Spain in the festive season for a one-off Christmas special. They’re back in the village of Moclin, where they spent a long, hot summer turning an old wreck into a dreamy B&B. Before they put the house on the market, they want to throw one final party to say thank you to all their friends who helped them with the project.
Reuniting with some old faces, Amanda and Alan reveal that they want to celebrate an Anglo-Spanish Christmas, which will culminate in them hosting a big feast at their Moclin home. Keen to learn what local festive traditions they can adopt, Alan suspects it will be a unique experience, while Amanda warns there will be a couple of their own British traditions thrown in for good measure.
After Alan professes a love of Christmas maximalism, Amanda worries that his festive decorating skills could be up there with his actual decorating skills. Not wanting anything clumsy this season, Amanda is all about a classy Christmas aesthetic when it comes to decorating their house. Unfortunately, Alan has other ideas as he heads to buy some tree decorations and gets carried away in the tinsel department.
With a menu to plan, the two friends swap their boiler suits for aprons. Alan invites over his favourite local, Marco the mayor, to help prepare his mum’s shrimp cocktail. But the mayor’s penchant for Tabasco nearly upends Alan’s precious recipe, and he has a job on his hands to keep his sous chef under control!
Meanwhile, Amanda is in charge of desserts and visits one of Granada’s oldest bakeries to learn about Spain’s famous three kings cake, where gifts are hidden and the finder of the king is rewarded with special treatment for the day. Not to be outdone by Spanish traditions, Amanda introduces the locals to her nan’s famous sherry trifle. Who better to help her than her favourite sherry man, Juan, who travels over from Jerez to assist? The two of them embrace the festive spirit, and their dinner guests are in for a treat as Amanda is especially liberal with the quantity of sherry mixed into the cream.
Away from the menu planning, the two best friends make the most of the Christmas season to enjoy other Andalusian delights.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.sub-title: Dundee - A Repair for a Scottish Football Legend ║ S1
programme.desc:
In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero.
Dom and Lucia are in Dundee, where regeneration of the waterfront has sparked change throughout the city. However, in the shadow of the celebrated RSS Discovery, Scotland’s oldest wooden ship, HMS Unicorn, is moored around the corner and a little neglected. Beloved by many, especially the generations of the Women's Royal Naval Service who trained on it, the 200-year-old vessel is in need of immediate preservation. However, getting it into dry dock is a costly operation, so the team are visiting to help with the fundraising efforts. In the past, a fibreglass copy of the unicorn figurehead went on tour to raise awareness of the project, but it has been unable to perform those duties since it was damaged a decade ago. Despite some recent health troubles, heraldic sculptor Peter is eager to repair the figurehead so that it can go out on its fundraising excursions once again.
It’s all to play for when Dom picks up a Scotland Schoolboys football cap that holds immense significance for Amanda. It was awarded to her husband Frank, who became a legend at local club Dundee United, playing there for a decade. But after retirement, Frank suffered from vascular dementia, and he would cradle the cap often, serving as a reminder of earlier days. Now, the gold brocade is tarnished, and the navy blue fabric faded, so master hatter Jayesh Vaghela has his work cut out to restore it to how it looked when Frank first held it all those years ago.

programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
The four chefs who have survived the intensity of the heats are back in the kitchen. Now they must prove to Marcus and Monica that they have the consistency, confidence and creativity to take on the next level of the competition.
First up is the invention test, where the chefs must put pistachio centre stage and show Marcus and Monica what they can do with it. It’s an ingredient that naturally lends itself to pastry and desserts, but used cleverly in a savoury dish, it could give one chef the edge. Will anyone dare to take it somewhere unexpected?
But the chefs aren’t finished yet. Their next test takes them out of the kitchen and into the company of three of the country’s most influential food critics: William Sitwell, Jimi Famurewa and, taking her place alongside them for the first time, Ixta Belfrage, a recipe developer and cookbook author who spent five years working at the Ottolenghi Test Kitchen.
The chefs must cook a two-course menu that showcases their food, ideas and technical ability, knowing that every element will be scrutinised by some of the toughest palates in the business. This is their chance to prove they can produce food that excites and surprises. However, impressing three professional critics is no easy feat, and their verdicts could have a major bearing on what happens next.
Back in the kitchen, Marcus and Monica must weigh up everything they have seen and tasted before deciding which chefs have done enough to progress. With only three places in knockout week available, one mistake, an underwhelming plate or a missed opportunity could make all the difference. Who will earn their place in the next stage – and whose journey ends here?
The pressure is mounting as the chefs edge closer to the coveted MasterChef: The Professionals title. Judge - Marcus Wareing Judge - Monica Galetti Series Editor - Antonia Lloyd Series Director - Emma Reynolds Executive Producer - Kelly Sparks Production Company - Shine TV.

programme.title: Escaping Idi Amin
programme.desc:
In August 1972, Idi Amin is 18 months into his dictatorship. Supporters hail the new president - a former boxer and soldier - as a saviour, and his rise to power is greeted with celebration and hope across Uganda.
But beneath the apparent social harmony, resentment runs deep. Until 1962, Uganda had been a protectorate of the British - with the British very much at the top of the pile, Africans at the bottom and Asians in the middle. Despite ten years of independence, many Africans feel that they are denied opportunities to improve their position in society. Idi Amin decides to exploit their feelings and increase support for his regime.
With one announcement from the president, the lives of 80,000 people in Uganda are changed forever. In a bid to cement his leadership, Idi Amin announces that all Ugandan Asians must leave the country within 90 days. Will they be able to flee on their British passports? programme.title: Great Coastal Railway Journeys
programme.desc:
Michael’s journey along the coast of Northumberland continues towards the Farne Islands, takes in the holy island of Lindisfarne, and finishes in England’s northernmost town, Berwick-upon-Tweed.
On the largest of the Farne Islands, Inner Farne, Michael pitches in to help rangers clear a toxic plant which is invading the island. It’s so prolific that it’s threatening the native plants upon which seabirds depend for nesting.
From the mainland, Michael sets off on a two-mile pilgrimage along a single-track causeway, which twice a day is covered by the North Sea. His destination is the holy island of Lindisfarne. Michael discovers that the island was chosen in the seventh century by St Aidan as the site for a monastery. Northumbria’s patron saint, St Cuthbert, later became bishop there. The vicar of the island today shows Michael a full-sized reproduction of the beautifully illuminated Lindisfarne Gospels, the originals of which are held in the British Museum.
Back on the East Coast Main Line, Michael hugs the North Sea coast, crossing the River Tweed on Robert Stephenson’s Royal Border Bridge to reach Britain’s most northern town, Berwick-upon-Tweed. Struck by the variety of accents and dialects in the north east, Michael learns what distinguishes a Geordie from a Smoggie.
Only two-and-a-half-miles from Scotland, Berwick-upon-Tweed has a turbulent past and an intriguing custom, dating back to the 15th century. Michael begs permission from the town’s mayor to join horses and riders in a ceremony to mark the border between Scotland and England along a line agreed in 1438. programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc:
This short documentary follows Kate Mobbs-Morgan and her trusty team of working horses. For centuries, horses formed an integral part of our working landscape. Kate is passionate about working horses and believes they still have a key role to play in today’s environment.
Kate trained in horticulture and always loved working with animals. In her late thirties, she was diagnosed with a rare cancer and had to undergo radical surgery. This prompted Kate to pursue a new career, combining her passion for working outdoors with her interest in working horses.
Almost two decades later, she has built her own working-horses business, specialising in forestry work and land management. She and her horses are brought in to work on sites where large machines cannot gain access or are not wanted, such as locations that are environmentally sensitive, steep terrain and wet ground.
Her horse-logging team is made up of: Kipp, the herd leader whom Kate has known since the day he was born but is now approaching retirement; Quinlan, who is powerful but suffers with anxiety; and Garth, a relatively new member of the team who has yet to start working full-time.
There was a fourth member of the team, Sol, who passed away suddenly last year, leaving Kate heartbroken and the herd out of balance. To restore the herd to full strength, Kate has just brought in a young mare named Brigid, but she is quite feisty, and it will take several years of patient training before she is ready to join the other working horses.
Kate knows that if there is to be a future for working horses, there needs to be people with the knowledge and skills to do the job. Alongside other professional horse loggers, Kate has started training new entrants into the industry.
The working-horse community is relatively small and is spread out across the country. Once a year, though, horse loggers come together to compete. In 2026, the competition is being held in Yorkshire. An obstacle course will test both horse and handler, with contests for single horses and pairs.
Kate takes her trusty steed Kipp and his anxious but sturdy companion Quinlan along to compete, but can she keep her own anxiety in check? Director - Luke Pavey Executive Producer - Anna Davies Editor - Al Edwards.

On 24th September 2025, the main road outside one of Bangkok's major hospitals collapsed. The giant sinkhole, the size of two tennis courts, snapped water pipes, ripped down power lines, and swallowed two vehicles.
During the day, it continued to grow, threatening the foundations of the hospital and forcing close to a thousand staff and patients to evacuate the building. Ampan Vimonvattana, vice dean of Vajira Hospital, witnessed the collapse: 'The earth swallowed everything... it pulled the road surface, the soil, anything on top. Even the electrical poles got dragged down. It was really scary.'
Why Sinkholes Collapse explores cases of sinkholes in Godstone, Surrey, a collapse under a main road in Yashio City in Japan and the underground quarries that are beneath ten per cent of Paris to help explain why sinkholes occur and how they can be prevented.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
A journey into the last great frontier on earth. Beneath the ocean's surface lies a vast, largely unknown realm of deep coral reefs, towering mountains, volcanoes and hydrothermal vents, all part of the largest living space on the planet. Once thought to be empty and inaccessible, this hidden world is now yielding its secrets. New technology, including remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), is taking us further into this realm than ever before, revealing an astonishing abundance of life and some of the most exciting discoveries of our time.
In the Pacific, a young female argonaut, no bigger than a garden pea, joins the greatest movement of life on earth. Every night, trillions of animals rise from the depths to feed near the surface. Unable to travel such immense distances alone, they have evolved an ingenious solution: hitchhiking aboard other animals as they journey through the open ocean.
As sunlight fades, the animals of the deep create light of their own - bioluminescence. A flash can lure prey, provide camouflage, warn an attacker or carry a message through the darkness. Yet much of this ancient language of living light remains a mystery.
Deeper still, beneath immense pressure and suspended in an apparently boundless expanse, life takes on extraordinary forms. Siphonophores drift through the darkness. Each may appear to be a single animal, but it is in fact an entire colony of specialised individuals working together. Some have remarkable body forms, including one which scientists describe as the ‘flying spaghetti monster’. Laser imaging systems are allowing scientists to study these extraordinarily delicate creatures, revealing their hidden lives in spectacular ways and discovering new species in the process.
On the seabed, seemingly endless plains give way to extraordinary worlds - if you follow the clues to find them. Methane escaping from deep beneath the sea floor creates oases of life in the Arctic. Forests of corals flourish in perpetual darkness, providing food and shelter for countless animals, with some colonies having survived for thousands of years. On a volcanic seamount off Canada, more than two million skate eggs blanket the summit, forming the largest deep sea nursery yet discovered.

programme.title: The Misadventures of Romesh Ranganathan
programme.desc:
In the final part of his African odyssey, Romesh travels to the fourth largest island in the world – Madagascar. But like most people, when he brings to mind this former French colony in the Indian Ocean, his only reference is an animated Disney film.
Romesh embarks on a mission, guided by exuberant diving instructor Bic, to find out what Madagascar has to offer the uninitiated - apart from cartoon dancing lemurs.
In the chaotic capital of Antananarivo, Bic samples a popular soup made from an eye-watering delicacy, Rom discovers that local taxi drivers have an intoxicating way of economising on fuel, and they admire breathtaking views from an impressive hilltop palace, once home to Madagascar’s notoriously brutal 'Mad Queen'.
Leaving the bustling capital behind, Bic is excited to show Rom the stunning coasts and national parks on the west side of the island, near where Bic grew up as part of the Vezu fishing tribe. Rom risks his life and dignity trying to hike vertical razor-sharp rocks and endures some of the worst roads in the world, but he is rewarded with a gastronomic hidden gem.
Rom and Bic encounter ancient baobab trees, sail traditional pirogue boats and visit a village shaman famed for channelling the spirits of long dead ancestors. There’s nothing for it but to go with the flow when their ferry is hijacked by a snake stowaway, and it’s love at first sight when Rom finally comes face to face with the legendary lemurs.
In Madagascar, Rom discovers there’s far more to the country than he had ever imagined. But he also learns that the diverse flora and fauna that are endemic to the island and its people face an unprecedented threat from climate change. programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
The final week of heats continues as another group of ambitious professional chefs steps up to prove they have the talent and technique to progress in the competition. But before they can look ahead, they must navigate two demanding challenges that will put their culinary skills and composure to the test.
First, it’s the skills test, where the chefs must fillet a sea bream and use it to create a shellfish risotto, finished with a spinach garnish. It’s a deceptively demanding dish, requiring sharp filleting skills to prepare the fish cleanly, precise timing to achieve perfectly cooked rice and the finesse to build a rich, balanced risotto without losing the delicate flavours of the seafood. Every element must come together seamlessly, with no room to hide behind elaborate presentation.
For some, the combination of intricate preparation and exacting technique proves daunting, leaving them struggling to keep pace. Others take the challenge in their stride, showing the confidence and control of seasoned professionals. Will the chefs’ efforts impress the judges, or will their shortcomings leave Marcus and Monica questioning whether they have what it takes to make it to the next stage?
With the skills test behind them, the chefs have the chance to show Marcus and Monica what they can do when given the freedom to cook their own food. In the signature dish round, they have 90 minutes to create a plate that reflects their personality, showcases their strengths and makes a compelling case for why they deserve to progress.
For some, it’s an opportunity to demonstrate real ambition and push their cooking in exciting new directions. For others, finding the right balance between ambition and execution proves more difficult.
The judges must decide whose cooking has made a strong enough impression to keep them in the running and whose journey ends here. programme.title: Escaping Idi Amin

In September 1972, one month after dictator Idi Amin announces his plan to expel all Ugandan Asians from the country, 80,000 people are making plans to flee, in fear for their lives. Maz and Bharti head for the capital Kampala, where hundreds gather, desperate to find out whether their British passports will be enough to escape to Britain.
As the deadline approaches, Harminder’s father escapes arrest and schoolboy Paresh hides during overnight curfews while gunfire echoes across the city.
Britain is divided. Controversial politician Enoch Powell rallies those who say the Ugandan Asians have no right to come, a newspaper poll finds just six per cent of the public want them here, and some councils try to steer new arrivals away from their cities.
In Uganda, Amin refuses to negotiate – stepping up the pressure on those stuck in the country. Five chefs remain in the race for a spot in the quarter-final, but first they must impress in two more challenges designed to test their creativity, precision and technical ability.
Marcus and Monica are joined by acclaimed South African chef Ash Valenzuela-Heeger, winner of the prestigious 2025 Michelin Young Chef Award. Her impressive career has seen her hone her craft at some of the world’s most celebrated restaurants, including London’s three-Michelin-starred Ledbury and Cape Town’s renowned Test Kitchen. She has since made her mark with Riverine Rabbit in Birmingham, which earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2025.
Known for her bold, inventive cooking, Ash draws on her South African heritage and international influences, with live-fire techniques at the heart of her culinary style. She challenges the chefs to cook BBQ beef sirloin, served with BBQ maitake mushrooms, caramelised roscoff onions and a cafe au lait sauce. It’s a brief that demands a sophisticated understanding of flavour, smoke and fire, and the ability to make every element work in harmony.
With the standard rising and a quarter-final place within reach, can the contestants deliver a plate worthy of this award-winning chef’s exacting standards?
The signature dessert round is the final hurdle, and the chefs must show that they have the range and imagination to compete with the very best. This is their chance to take risks, bring their own ideas to the plate and prove that they can deliver something truly memorable. But sweet cooking demands a different kind of judgement; flavours must work in harmony, textures need to complement one another, and the finishing touches can make all the difference between a good dessert and a great one.
Marcus and Monica have seen what the chefs can do with savoury ingredients, but now they must decide who has the finesse and creative flair to progress to the next stage of the competition. As the final plates are tasted, will the desserts be enough to secure a place in the quarter-final? And whose MasterChef journey must come to an end? programme.title: MasterChef: The Professionals
programme.desc:
It’s the last quarter-final of the series, and with a place in knockout week at stake, there’s everything to play for. Four chefs return to the kitchen knowing that one false move could bring their ambitions to an abrupt end. Marcus and Monica are looking for the consistency, ingenuity and confidence that mark out a truly exceptional chef.
First up is the invention test, and the secret ingredient has a history stretching back more than 2,000 years: miso. A staple of Japanese cuisine, this fermented paste brings extraordinary depth, savoury complexity and umami to a dish. With different varieties offering their own distinctive flavours, the chefs must work out how best to make miso the star of the plate. Who will turn this humble ingredient into something exceptional, and who will fall short of expectations?
Then they face one last chance to prove they have what it takes to go all the way.
Three highly respected food writers and critics, Tom Parker Bowles, Leyla Kazim and Jimi Famurewa, wait to put the chefs’ cooking under the microscope. Between them, they’ve eaten at restaurants around the world and very little escapes their attention. They know what exceptional food looks, tastes and feels like, and they’ll be looking beyond technical skill to the details that separate a good meal from a truly memorable one.
The chefs must serve up a two-course menu that captures their culinary identity, showcases their abilities and gives these exacting critics something to talk about. Every choice matters, from the balance of flavours to the smallest finishing touch. Can they cook with enough originality and precision to make a lasting impression?
Back in the kitchen, Marcus and Monica face their biggest decision yet. With the quarter-finals coming to a close and only three places in knockout week up for grabs, they must consider the chefs’ performances across the challenges before deciding who has done enough to progress to the next stage. For those who fall short, there will be no second chance.
Who will take the next step towards the coveted MasterChef: The Professionals title, and whose journey ends at the final hurdle?

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc:
In the series finale, the teams race nearly 2,000km to the finish line on the southern edge of mainland Australia and the country’s cultural capital, Melbourne. This is the longest and potentially most expensive leg of the race so far.
As teams battle it out, every minute counts. Weeks of racing culminate in a battle of brains, budget and luck where even the smallest delay could cost them. On reaching Melbourne, the racers face a final sprint across the bustling city. Navigating traffic, trams and towering buildings, the teams must push to the very last minute to reach the finish line atop a modern-day Colosseum.
After 7,500km across countries and continents, which team will triumph and be the first to sign the all-important book and be crowned the winners of Celebrity Race Across the World? programme.title: Farm 999
programme.sub-title: Inferno in the Fields and the Fight to Save Badgers ║ S1E2/15
programme.desc:
In Bedfordshire, a scorching summer’s day turns to chaos when flames rip through the countryside. Farmers and firefighters join forces in a desperate battle to contain a fast-moving field fire threatening homes and livelihoods. With dramatic footage filmed by farmer and YouTuber George Saunders, we hear first-hand from those who faced the blaze – including the crews who risked everything to stop it from spreading.
In Leicestershire, a beloved horse is in danger after plunging into a freezing swimming pool. As panic rises, a specialist fire and rescue team race to save it, with the help of a local farmer, before it’s too late.
Meanwhile, reporter Paul Colgan is in Northern Ireland to meet volunteers behind Operation Brockwatch – a groundbreaking scheme using hidden cameras to protect badgers from ruthless illegal hunters. Producer - Richard Weller Director - Richard Weller Executive Producer - Tracie O’Neill.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc:
Antiques meet archaeology in this episode from West Sussex. In the village of Fishbourne, Natasha Raskin Sharp learns about the discovery of a huge Roman palace by workmen in the 1960s. In the company of curator Dr Rob Symmons, she hears how part of the palace and its treasures were unearthed over eight summers by hundreds of volunteers. One of the highlights is an exquisite mosaic featuring mythical sea creatures around which the owner – a high-ranking Roman – and his guests would have sat to eat meals. Another highlight is a partially smashed statue of Emperor Nero and a remarkably rare rabbit bone.
Hoping to unearth their own treasures are two teams of bargain hunters at Ardingly antiques fair. In blue are cousins Michelle and Emma, and in red are golfing pals Linda and Yvonne. With expert Caroline Hawley by their side, the reds get off to an explosive start, eyeing up a pair of powder flasks. Meanwhile, Emma spots a West German pottery vase, but expert Thomas Forrester doubts that profits will bloom at auction.
Wielding his gavel at the auction is Nick Hall; can the experts’ bonus buys bring home the big bucks? programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
When a burnt-out delivery van is discovered on a quiet rural road, Rose and Raj are met with a grim crime scene: a charred body in the passenger seat and no sign of the driver. Sifting through the ashes, they uncover a bizarre assortment of clues, including a melted key fob, rusted gardening tools and a bottle of imported Polish vodka.
Tracking down the van’s insured drivers leads them to Kelly Prudham, a tight-lipped agency cleaner, and Scott Smith, a devoted widowed father missing since the previous evening. Is Scott the vanished driver, or is he the unidentified victim in the passenger seat? Kelly claims concern for Scott’s young daughter Chloe, yet she stonewalls every question. However, Rose’s sharp eyes spot an identical bottle of Polish vodka in Kelly’s flat, indicating that Kelly may have a dangerous motive for concealing her and Scott’s recent movements.
Meanwhile, Joe can’t resist probing into the mystery. Dragging Brother Christopher along, he snoops around the crime scene and dives into Scott’s past. Relying on his sharp human intuition and feeling somewhat aligned with this man who seems to be struggling as a father, Joe forms a bold theory about Scott’s whereabouts. But his covert search goes sideways, stranding Joe and Christopher in a perilous predicament deep in the Northumbrian moors.
With time running out and danger escalating, Rose, Joe and Raj must pool their findings to identify the burnt remains, track down the arsonist and expose the motive behind the blaze before the truth burns out completely. programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.sub-title: East Lothian - Saving the Musselburgh Carriage ║ S1
programme.desc:
In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero.
Will and Kirsten are in Musselburgh, on Scotland’s east coast. It’s a town boasting a proud heritage that is celebrated each year with a procession led by their elected Honest Lad and Honest Lass. However, for the past few years, the antique carriage these local luminaries ride in has been off the road. Restoring the carriage is a huge job that requires the skills of local signwriter Ross Hastie and wheelwright Greg Rowland, and made more complicated by the impending deadline of this year’s festival.
It's a bit of a musical mystery when the team are faced with Erica’s Stroviol. In the family since the 1930s, it belonged to Erica's father, who was a passionate musician who played in several local groups. The distinctive horn has become detached from this turn-of-the-century musical oddity, so it might take more than just the skills of stringed instrument expert Becky Houghton to get a tune out of it once again.
In nearby Edinburgh, Will stops off at Stewart Christie & Co, Scotland’s oldest bespoke tailors, to discover how their handmade tweed clothes balance modern demands with century-old techniques. Will gets an insight into every step of the process, from an initial measuring to getting on the scissors himself and cutting out his own waistcoat pattern from the tweed cloth the company built their name on. programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc:
With exclusive access to the police service on the paradise island of Bermuda, we follow life on the front line for the near 400 officers keeping both holidaymakers and locals safe. From patrols and traffic operations to the drug unit, forensics, tactical response teams, the coastguard and community policing, the series goes behind the scenes with the officers at the heart of the action.
The island has its fair share of challenges on both land and sea, with more than 3,000 crimes committed each year. We show how these dedicated officers, including around 30 from the UK, deal with the highs and lows of policing this British Overseas Territory.
In the centre of the island, Sergeant Milton Hill responds to reports of an elderly man walking along a busy roadside in clear distress. When he arrives, the man is unable to recall his name, address or basic personal details, and the mystery begins. Concerned for his safety, Milton stays close, guiding traffic around him as he repeatedly steps into the road. On an island where everyone knows everyone, Officer Milton sends a photograph of the man to base, where his identity provides a surprising twist to the tale. It's a race against time for Officer Milton to get him returned home safely.
Elsewhere, PC Eddie Smith and PC Jameela Sabir are on a stop-and-search operation. When Sergeant Mervin Homer examines a bike, he discovers a dangerous switchblade hidden under the seat. With the rider offering no feasible explanation, the prohibited weapon is immediately seized. Back at Hamilton Police Station, Custody Sergeant Francis Blackman reads the bike rider their rights, while Assistant Commissioner Martin Weekes examines other recently confiscated blades, including machetes and a samurai sword.
At Bermuda’s international airport, PC Paul 'Geordie' Watson supports Customs Officer Malcolm Martin and drugs dog Zorro while screening an incoming flight from Canada. After sweeping the aircraft cabin in just five minutes, Zorro indicates interest in two bags in the arrivals hall, leaving customs officers the job of discreetly monitoring the family before searching their bags and bringing them in for questioning. What will the canine team uncover next?

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
Claire McCollum is in Glasgow to celebrate Advent Sunday, a special time of waiting for Christ’s arrival, and St Andrew’s Day to see how Scotland’s patron saint continues to inspire Christians today.
At the magnificent St Andrew’s Cathedral, Claire explores the story of Scotland’s patron saint with theologian and Quaker Alastair McIntosh. Originally a fisherman, Andrew was among the first disciples called by Jesus and went on to dedicate his life to spreading Christ’s message.
Today, that same spirit of Christian faith and service can be seen at Glasgow City Mission, a Christian charity that has supported people on the margins of society for 200 years, offering rehabilitation support, creative classes and hot meals.
Among those making a difference is support worker Angela Wilson, who first came to the charity for help 25 years ago. As Claire discovers more about the mission’s work, she meets some of its guests, visits its art class and choir, and hears how the charity has transformed lives. Together, they explore how the mission seeks to embody the Advent themes of hope, peace, joy and love.
The story comes full circle at Troon Harbour, where the Fishermen’s Mission continues St Andrew’s legacy of supporting those who make their living at sea. Area officer Louise Liddell explains how the organisation offers practical, financial and faith-based support to fishermen and their families throughout their lives.
With music to celebrate Advent Sunday and St Andrew’s Day, including a new recording from Celtic Worship.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
In the frozen waters of the Arctic, a bowhead whale breaks the sea ice with its skull to breathe - completely at home in this seemingly hostile sea. Polar waters may seem remote, but their influence supports more than the wildlife that thrives there by helping to power a global system of ocean currents that creates extraordinary opportunities for wildlife far beyond the ice.
In the Falkland Islands, nutrient-rich water flowing north from Antarctica sustains a colony of king penguins. But returning parents weighed down with food for their chicks must try to cross a beach patrolled by an extraordinary southern sea lion, the only one known to regularly hunt king penguins on land.
Cold water from the Arctic also travels thousands of miles. In the Pacific, it cools the coast of Japan, where a male dwarf lumpsucker, about the size of a pea, must find a nest and persuade a female to enter. Once she has laid her eggs, he becomes a devoted single father, guarding them from hungry predators for 40 days and nights.
Around Antarctica, hundreds of fin whales converge on one of the greatest feeding grounds on earth. They work together in a spectacular synchronised formation, turning clockwise before lunging onto their sides to feast on Antarctic krill. Beneath the continent’s sea ice lies a remarkable world where giant sea spiders clamber over ancient glass sponges and a tiny amphipod escapes hungry icefish by hitching a ride on sea angels and venomous jellyfish.
The influence of the polar waters is so strong that it helps power global currents that cross entire oceans and circle the planet. In the North Atlantic, the Gulf Stream brings warm water from the Caribbean to the shores of Britain, attracting Atlantic bluefin tuna to hunt off the Cornish coast. These powerful predators, which can attack at 45 miles per hour, have only recently returned to British shores following international action to protect them.
But the currents all these animals rely on are changing. With a loss of sea ice, many are now weakening, driving animals to adapt – sometimes in surprising ways. Around Newfoundland, green sea urchins are losing the kelp forests that once protected them from the sun’s ultraviolet rays.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc:
Matt Baker and Margherita Taylor visit RSPB Freiston Shore in Lincolnshire to see an ambitious engineering project being unveiled - a saline lagoon created to provide an ecologically important habitat alongside the Wash.
Matt meets the team behind the project to discover how they turned a 17-acre site into a highly engineered coastal lagoon, creating vital nesting sites for migratory birds. He also peers beneath the surface to see what saline specialists have already colonised in this new habitat.
Margherita joins the volunteers preparing the lagoon’s nesting sites ahead of the spring breeding season, while Adam Henson is in Belfast for the BBC Food and Farming Awards to reveal Countryfile’s Young Countryside Champion 2026. programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.sub-title: Swanage Pier and Seafront, Dorset 3 ║ S46
programme.desc:
The roadshow pays a final visit to Swanage Pier in Dorset, where treasures include shipwreck finds, a jewel-encrusted bird, an early folding bike and a pair of aviator boots with a link to a tragic wartime mission.
Ronnie Archer-Morgan is moved by a powerful sculpture from South Africa, while Serhat Ahmet celebrates trailblazing potter Hannah Barlow when he sees a rare example of her artistry in ceramics. Siobhan Tyrrell sees items of motoring memorabilia that belonged to pioneering female driver Ivy Cummings, while Geoffrey Munn is dazzled by a jewel-encrusted brooch in the shape of a mysterious bird.
Mark Hill admires the engineering that has gone into a homemade folding bike, while Mark Smith is moved to tears by a pair of aviator’s boots that have a link to a tragic wartime mission that involved his late father. Marc Allum meets members of a local diving group and is intrigued to see a collection of First World War keepsakes salvaged from the wreck of the Kyrra, sunk by a German U-boat in May 1918, while Justin Croft sees a thrilling first-hand survivor’s account of a much earlier shipwreck.
Fiona finds out about the history of the Swanage lifeboat and the wider history of the RNLI, which is marking its bicentenary, and tries to put three ancient fossils in order of age in a quirky geological challenge set by Marc Allum. programme.title: Heal with the Princess of Wales
programme.desc:
Introduced by Kirsty Young
Acquired for the BBC, the Princess’s deeply personal film explores life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.
It follows the Princess on a journey through some of Britain's most spectacular landscapes as she undertakes the National Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales, to meet her family at the finish line.
Set against the backdrop of the challenge itself, the Princess reflects on her own experience alongside individuals navigating their own health journeys. Together, they explore the profound impact serious illness can have on the whole person, and the people, places and experiences that can help us heal.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
A journey into the last great frontier on earth. Beneath the ocean's surface lies a vast, largely unknown realm of deep coral reefs, towering mountains, volcanoes and hydrothermal vents, all part of the largest living space on the planet. Once thought to be empty and inaccessible, this hidden world is now yielding its secrets. New technology, including remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), is taking us further into this realm than ever before, revealing an astonishing abundance of life and some of the most exciting discoveries of our time.
In the Pacific, a young female argonaut, no bigger than a garden pea, joins the greatest movement of life on earth. Every night, trillions of animals rise from the depths to feed near the surface. Unable to travel such immense distances alone, they have evolved an ingenious solution: hitchhiking aboard other animals as they journey through the open ocean.
As sunlight fades, the animals of the deep create light of their own - bioluminescence. A flash can lure prey, provide camouflage, warn an attacker or carry a message through the darkness. Yet much of this ancient language of living light remains a mystery.
Deeper still, beneath immense pressure and suspended in an apparently boundless expanse, life takes on extraordinary forms. Siphonophores drift through the darkness. Each may appear to be a single animal, but it is in fact an entire colony of specialised individuals working together. Some have remarkable body forms, including one which scientists describe as the ‘flying spaghetti monster’. Laser imaging systems are allowing scientists to study these extraordinarily delicate creatures, revealing their hidden lives in spectacular ways and discovering new species in the process.
On the seabed, seemingly endless plains give way to extraordinary worlds - if you follow the clues to find them. Methane escaping from deep beneath the sea floor creates oases of life in the Arctic. Forests of corals flourish in perpetual darkness, providing food and shelter for countless animals, with some colonies having survived for thousands of years. On a volcanic seamount off Canada, more than two million skate eggs blanket the summit, forming the largest deep sea nursery yet discovered.

programme.title: Amanda & Alan's Spanish Job
programme.desc:
Best friends Amanda and Alan return to Spain in the festive season for a one-off Christmas special. They’re back in the village of Moclin, where they spent a long, hot summer turning an old wreck into a dreamy B&B. Before they put the house on the market, they want to throw one final party to say thank you to all their friends who helped them with the project.
Reuniting with some old faces, Amanda and Alan reveal that they want to celebrate an Anglo-Spanish Christmas, which will culminate in them hosting a big feast at their Moclin home. Keen to learn what local festive traditions they can adopt, Alan suspects it will be a unique experience, while Amanda warns there will be a couple of their own British traditions thrown in for good measure.
After Alan professes a love of Christmas maximalism, Amanda worries that his festive decorating skills could be up there with his actual decorating skills. Not wanting anything clumsy this season, Amanda is all about a classy Christmas aesthetic when it comes to decorating their house. Unfortunately, Alan has other ideas as he heads to buy some tree decorations and gets carried away in the tinsel department.
With a menu to plan, the two friends swap their boiler suits for aprons. Alan invites over his favourite local, Marco the mayor, to help prepare his mum’s shrimp cocktail. But the mayor’s penchant for Tabasco nearly upends Alan’s precious recipe, and he has a job on his hands to keep his sous chef under control!
Meanwhile, Amanda is in charge of desserts and visits one of Granada’s oldest bakeries to learn about Spain’s famous three kings cake, where gifts are hidden and the finder of the king is rewarded with special treatment for the day. Not to be outdone by Spanish traditions, Amanda introduces the locals to her nan’s famous sherry trifle. Who better to help her than her favourite sherry man, Juan, who travels over from Jerez to assist? The two of them embrace the festive spirit, and their dinner guests are in for a treat as Amanda is especially liberal with the quantity of sherry mixed into the cream.
Away from the menu planning, the two best friends make the most of the Christmas season to enjoy other Andalusian delights.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.sub-title: Dundee - A Repair for a Scottish Football Legend ║ S1
programme.desc:
In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero.
Dom and Lucia are in Dundee, where regeneration of the waterfront has sparked change throughout the city. However, in the shadow of the celebrated RSS Discovery, Scotland’s oldest wooden ship, HMS Unicorn, is moored around the corner and a little neglected. Beloved by many, especially the generations of the Women's Royal Naval Service who trained on it, the 200-year-old vessel is in need of immediate preservation. However, getting it into dry dock is a costly operation, so the team are visiting to help with the fundraising efforts. In the past, a fibreglass copy of the unicorn figurehead went on tour to raise awareness of the project, but it has been unable to perform those duties since it was damaged a decade ago. Despite some recent health troubles, heraldic sculptor Peter is eager to repair the figurehead so that it can go out on its fundraising excursions once again.
It’s all to play for when Dom picks up a Scotland Schoolboys football cap that holds immense significance for Amanda. It was awarded to her husband Frank, who became a legend at local club Dundee United, playing there for a decade. But after retirement, Frank suffered from vascular dementia, and he would cradle the cap often, serving as a reminder of earlier days. Now, the gold brocade is tarnished, and the navy blue fabric faded, so master hatter Jayesh Vaghela has his work cut out to restore it to how it looked when Frank first held it all those years ago.
Lucia trained at the V&A in London, but this is her chance to visit the Dundee branch of the celebrated art and design museum. She is there to learn about their restoration of a lost Charles Rennie Mackintosh-designed interior. Originally in Miss Cranston’s Ingram Street Tearooms in Glasgow, the interior was painstakingly moved and rebuilt in Dundee. Bringing a work like this out of storage and back to the public is a conservator’s dream, and Lucia can’t wait to hear all about it.

The second group of five professional chefs step out of the MasterChef kitchen and into the competitive world of pop-up dining.

programme.desc:
Antiques meet archaeology in this episode from West Sussex. In the village of Fishbourne, Natasha Raskin Sharp learns about the discovery of a huge Roman palace by workmen in the 1960s. In the company of curator Dr Rob Symmons, she hears how part of the palace and its treasures were unearthed over eight summers by hundreds of volunteers. One of the highlights is an exquisite mosaic featuring mythical sea creatures around which the owner – a high-ranking Roman – and his guests would have sat to eat meals. Another highlight is a partially smashed statue of Emperor Nero and a remarkably rare rabbit bone.
Hoping to unearth their own treasures are two teams of bargain hunters at Ardingly antiques fair. In blue are cousins Michelle and Emma, and in red are golfing pals Linda and Yvonne. With expert Caroline Hawley by their side, the reds get off to an explosive start, eyeing up a pair of powder flasks. Meanwhile, Emma spots a West German pottery vase, but expert Thomas Forrester doubts that profits will bloom at auction.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
When a burnt-out delivery van is discovered on a quiet rural road, Rose and Raj are met with a grim crime scene: a charred body in the passenger seat and no sign of the driver. Sifting through the ashes, they uncover a bizarre assortment of clues, including a melted key fob, rusted gardening tools and a bottle of imported Polish vodka.
Tracking down the van’s insured drivers leads them to Kelly Prudham, a tight-lipped agency cleaner, and Scott Smith, a devoted widowed father missing since the previous evening. Is Scott the vanished driver, or is he the unidentified victim in the passenger seat? Kelly claims concern for Scott’s young daughter Chloe, yet she stonewalls every question. However, Rose’s sharp eyes spot an identical bottle of Polish vodka in Kelly’s flat, indicating that Kelly may have a dangerous motive for concealing her and Scott’s recent movements.
Meanwhile, Joe can’t resist probing into the mystery. Dragging Brother Christopher along, he snoops around the crime scene and dives into Scott’s past. Relying on his sharp human intuition and feeling somewhat aligned with this man who seems to be struggling as a father, Joe forms a bold theory about Scott’s whereabouts. But his covert search goes sideways, stranding Joe and Christopher in a perilous predicament deep in the Northumbrian moors.
With time running out and danger escalating, Rose, Joe and Raj must pool their findings to identify the burnt remains, track down the arsonist and expose the motive behind the blaze before the truth burns out completely. programme.title: Policing Paradise
programme.desc:
With exclusive access to the police service on the paradise island of Bermuda, we follow life on the front line for the near 400 officers keeping both holidaymakers and locals safe. From patrols and traffic operations to the drug unit, forensics, tactical response teams, the coastguard and community policing, the series goes behind the scenes with the officers at the heart of the action.
The island has its fair share of challenges on both land and sea, with more than 3,000 crimes committed each year. We show how these dedicated officers, including around 30 from the UK, deal with the highs and lows of policing this British Overseas Territory.
In the centre of the island, Sergeant Milton Hill responds to reports of an elderly man walking along a busy roadside in clear distress. When he arrives, the man is unable to recall his name, address or basic personal details, and the mystery begins. Concerned for his safety, Milton stays close, guiding traffic around him as he repeatedly steps into the road. On an island where everyone knows everyone, Officer Milton sends a photograph of the man to base, where his identity provides a surprising twist to the tale. It's a race against time for Officer Milton to get him returned home safely.
Elsewhere, PC Eddie Smith and PC Jameela Sabir are on a stop-and-search operation. When Sergeant Mervin Homer examines a bike, he discovers a dangerous switchblade hidden under the seat. With the rider offering no feasible explanation, the prohibited weapon is immediately seized. Back at Hamilton Police Station, Custody Sergeant Francis Blackman reads the bike rider their rights, while Assistant Commissioner Martin Weekes examines other recently confiscated blades, including machetes and a samurai sword.
At Bermuda’s international airport, PC Paul 'Geordie' Watson supports Customs Officer Malcolm Martin and drugs dog Zorro while screening an incoming flight from Canada. After sweeping the aircraft cabin in just five minutes, Zorro indicates interest in two bags in the arrivals hall, leaving customs officers the job of discreetly monitoring the family before searching their bags and bringing them in for questioning. What will the canine team uncover next?
