programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
Claire McCollum is in Glasgow to celebrate Advent Sunday, a special time of waiting for Christ’s arrival, and St Andrew’s Day to see how Scotland’s patron saint continues to inspire Christians today.
At the magnificent St Andrew’s Cathedral, Claire explores the story of Scotland’s patron saint with theologian and Quaker Alastair McIntosh. Originally a fisherman, Andrew was among the first disciples called by Jesus and went on to dedicate his life to spreading Christ’s message.
Today, that same spirit of Christian faith and service can be seen at Glasgow City Mission, a Christian charity that has supported people on the margins of society for 200 years, offering rehabilitation support, creative classes and hot meals.
Among those making a difference is support worker Angela Wilson, who first came to the charity for help 25 years ago. As Claire discovers more about the mission’s work, she meets some of its guests, visits its art class and choir, and hears how the charity has transformed lives. Together, they explore how the mission seeks to embody the Advent themes of hope, peace, joy and love.
The story comes full circle at Troon Harbour, where the Fishermen’s Mission continues St Andrew’s legacy of supporting those who make their living at sea. Area officer Louise Liddell explains how the organisation offers practical, financial and faith-based support to fishermen and their families throughout their lives.
With music to celebrate Advent Sunday and St Andrew’s Day, including a new recording from Celtic Worship.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
In the frozen waters of the Arctic, a bowhead whale breaks the sea ice with its skull to breathe - completely at home in this seemingly hostile sea. Polar waters may seem remote, but their influence supports more than the wildlife that thrives there by helping to power a global system of ocean currents that creates extraordinary opportunities for wildlife far beyond the ice.
In the Falkland Islands, nutrient-rich water flowing north from Antarctica sustains a colony of king penguins. But returning parents weighed down with food for their chicks must try to cross a beach patrolled by an extraordinary southern sea lion, the only one known to regularly hunt king penguins on land.
Cold water from the Arctic also travels thousands of miles. In the Pacific, it cools the coast of Japan, where a male dwarf lumpsucker, about the size of a pea, must find a nest and persuade a female to enter. Once she has laid her eggs, he becomes a devoted single father, guarding them from hungry predators for 40 days and nights.
Around Antarctica, hundreds of fin whales converge on one of the greatest feeding grounds on earth. They work together in a spectacular synchronised formation, turning clockwise before lunging onto their sides to feast on Antarctic krill. Beneath the continent’s sea ice lies a remarkable world where giant sea spiders clamber over ancient glass sponges and a tiny amphipod escapes hungry icefish by hitching a ride on sea angels and venomous jellyfish.
The influence of the polar waters is so strong that it helps power global currents that cross entire oceans and circle the planet. In the North Atlantic, the Gulf Stream brings warm water from the Caribbean to the shores of Britain, attracting Atlantic bluefin tuna to hunt off the Cornish coast. These powerful predators, which can attack at 45 miles per hour, have only recently returned to British shores following international action to protect them.
But the currents all these animals rely on are changing. With a loss of sea ice, many are now weakening, driving animals to adapt – sometimes in surprising ways. Around Newfoundland, green sea urchins are losing the kelp forests that once protected them from the sun’s ultraviolet rays.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc:
Matt Baker and Margherita Taylor visit RSPB Freiston Shore in Lincolnshire to see an ambitious engineering project being unveiled - a saline lagoon created to provide an ecologically important habitat alongside the Wash.
Matt meets the team behind the project to discover how they turned a 17-acre site into a highly engineered coastal lagoon, creating vital nesting sites for migratory birds. He also peers beneath the surface to see what saline specialists have already colonised in this new habitat.
Margherita joins the volunteers preparing the lagoon’s nesting sites ahead of the spring breeding season, while Adam Henson is in Belfast for the BBC Food and Farming Awards to reveal Countryfile’s Young Countryside Champion 2026. programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.sub-title: Swanage Pier and Seafront, Dorset 3 ║ S46
programme.desc:
The roadshow pays a final visit to Swanage Pier in Dorset, where treasures include shipwreck finds, a jewel-encrusted bird, an early folding bike and a pair of aviator boots with a link to a tragic wartime mission.
Ronnie Archer-Morgan is moved by a powerful sculpture from South Africa, while Serhat Ahmet celebrates trailblazing potter Hannah Barlow when he sees a rare example of her artistry in ceramics. Siobhan Tyrrell sees items of motoring memorabilia that belonged to pioneering female driver Ivy Cummings, while Geoffrey Munn is dazzled by a jewel-encrusted brooch in the shape of a mysterious bird.
Mark Hill admires the engineering that has gone into a homemade folding bike, while Mark Smith is moved to tears by a pair of aviator’s boots that have a link to a tragic wartime mission that involved his late father. Marc Allum meets members of a local diving group and is intrigued to see a collection of First World War keepsakes salvaged from the wreck of the Kyrra, sunk by a German U-boat in May 1918, while Justin Croft sees a thrilling first-hand survivor’s account of a much earlier shipwreck.
Fiona finds out about the history of the Swanage lifeboat and the wider history of the RNLI, which is marking its bicentenary, and tries to put three ancient fossils in order of age in a quirky geological challenge set by Marc Allum. programme.title: Heal with the Princess of Wales
programme.desc:
Introduced by Kirsty Young
Acquired for the BBC, the Princess’s deeply personal film explores life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.
It follows the Princess on a journey through some of Britain's most spectacular landscapes as she undertakes the National Three Peaks Challenge, climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales, to meet her family at the finish line.
Set against the backdrop of the challenge itself, the Princess reflects on her own experience alongside individuals navigating their own health journeys. Together, they explore the profound impact serious illness can have on the whole person, and the people, places and experiences that can help us heal.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc:
A journey into the last great frontier on earth. Beneath the ocean's surface lies a vast, largely unknown realm of deep coral reefs, towering mountains, volcanoes and hydrothermal vents, all part of the largest living space on the planet. Once thought to be empty and inaccessible, this hidden world is now yielding its secrets. New technology, including remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), is taking us further into this realm than ever before, revealing an astonishing abundance of life and some of the most exciting discoveries of our time.
In the Pacific, a young female argonaut, no bigger than a garden pea, joins the greatest movement of life on earth. Every night, trillions of animals rise from the depths to feed near the surface. Unable to travel such immense distances alone, they have evolved an ingenious solution: hitchhiking aboard other animals as they journey through the open ocean.
As sunlight fades, the animals of the deep create light of their own - bioluminescence. A flash can lure prey, provide camouflage, warn an attacker or carry a message through the darkness. Yet much of this ancient language of living light remains a mystery.
Deeper still, beneath immense pressure and suspended in an apparently boundless expanse, life takes on extraordinary forms. Siphonophores drift through the darkness. Each may appear to be a single animal, but it is in fact an entire colony of specialised individuals working together. Some have remarkable body forms, including one which scientists describe as the ‘flying spaghetti monster’. Laser imaging systems are allowing scientists to study these extraordinarily delicate creatures, revealing their hidden lives in spectacular ways and discovering new species in the process.
On the seabed, seemingly endless plains give way to extraordinary worlds - if you follow the clues to find them. Methane escaping from deep beneath the sea floor creates oases of life in the Arctic. Forests of corals flourish in perpetual darkness, providing food and shelter for countless animals, with some colonies having survived for thousands of years. On a volcanic seamount off Canada, more than two million skate eggs blanket the summit, forming the largest deep sea nursery yet discovered.

programme.title: Amanda & Alan's Spanish Job
programme.desc:
Best friends Amanda and Alan return to Spain in the festive season for a one-off Christmas special. They’re back in the village of Moclin, where they spent a long, hot summer turning an old wreck into a dreamy B&B. Before they put the house on the market, they want to throw one final party to say thank you to all their friends who helped them with the project.
Reuniting with some old faces, Amanda and Alan reveal that they want to celebrate an Anglo-Spanish Christmas, which will culminate in them hosting a big feast at their Moclin home. Keen to learn what local festive traditions they can adopt, Alan suspects it will be a unique experience, while Amanda warns there will be a couple of their own British traditions thrown in for good measure.
After Alan professes a love of Christmas maximalism, Amanda worries that his festive decorating skills could be up there with his actual decorating skills. Not wanting anything clumsy this season, Amanda is all about a classy Christmas aesthetic when it comes to decorating their house. Unfortunately, Alan has other ideas as he heads to buy some tree decorations and gets carried away in the tinsel department.
With a menu to plan, the two friends swap their boiler suits for aprons. Alan invites over his favourite local, Marco the mayor, to help prepare his mum’s shrimp cocktail. But the mayor’s penchant for Tabasco nearly upends Alan’s precious recipe, and he has a job on his hands to keep his sous chef under control!
Meanwhile, Amanda is in charge of desserts and visits one of Granada’s oldest bakeries to learn about Spain’s famous three kings cake, where gifts are hidden and the finder of the king is rewarded with special treatment for the day. Not to be outdone by Spanish traditions, Amanda introduces the locals to her nan’s famous sherry trifle. Who better to help her than her favourite sherry man, Juan, who travels over from Jerez to assist? The two of them embrace the festive spirit, and their dinner guests are in for a treat as Amanda is especially liberal with the quantity of sherry mixed into the cream.
Away from the menu planning, the two best friends make the most of the Christmas season to enjoy other Andalusian delights.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.sub-title: Dundee - A Repair for a Scottish Football Legend ║ S1
programme.desc:
In this episode, the experts lend their skills to a community project, hear the story behind a new treasure to be repaired and visit a local crafting hero.
Dom and Lucia are in Dundee, where regeneration of the waterfront has sparked change throughout the city. However, in the shadow of the celebrated RSS Discovery, Scotland’s oldest wooden ship, HMS Unicorn, is moored around the corner and a little neglected. Beloved by many, especially the generations of the Women's Royal Naval Service who trained on it, the 200-year-old vessel is in need of immediate preservation. However, getting it into dry dock is a costly operation, so the team are visiting to help with the fundraising efforts. In the past, a fibreglass copy of the unicorn figurehead went on tour to raise awareness of the project, but it has been unable to perform those duties since it was damaged a decade ago. Despite some recent health troubles, heraldic sculptor Peter is eager to repair the figurehead so that it can go out on its fundraising excursions once again.
It’s all to play for when Dom picks up a Scotland Schoolboys football cap that holds immense significance for Amanda. It was awarded to her husband Frank, who became a legend at local club Dundee United, playing there for a decade. But after retirement, Frank suffered from vascular dementia, and he would cradle the cap often, serving as a reminder of earlier days. Now, the gold brocade is tarnished, and the navy blue fabric faded, so master hatter Jayesh Vaghela has his work cut out to restore it to how it looked when Frank first held it all those years ago.
Lucia trained at the V&A in London, but this is her chance to visit the Dundee branch of the celebrated art and design museum. She is there to learn about their restoration of a lost Charles Rennie Mackintosh-designed interior. Originally in Miss Cranston’s Ingram Street Tearooms in Glasgow, the interior was painstakingly moved and rebuilt in Dundee. Bringing a work like this out of storage and back to the public is a conservator’s dream, and Lucia can’t wait to hear all about it.

programme.title: Planet Earth II
programme.desc: Remote islands offer sanctuary for some of the planet's strangest and rarest creatures. The rare pygmy three-toed sloth enjoys a peaceful existence on an idyllic Caribbean island, while nesting albatross thrive in predator free isolation. However, island life always comes at a cost. On the Galapagos Islands young marine iguana must escape an onslaught of deadly racer snakes the moment they hatch from the sand. David Attenborough - Narrator.

programme.title: Planet Earth II
programme.desc: The great mountain ranges are some of the planet's most spectacular landscapes, but they are unforgiving places to live in. Only few pioneering animals have what it takes to endure at extreme altitude. Mountain animals are also amongst the most elusive in the world, yet this film provides unique and intimate glimpses into their secretive lives. Witness the moment four snow leopards come together when a mother and cub become trapped between two rival males. David Attenborough - Narrator.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E1 ║ Warrington to Preston ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: Armed with his early 20th century Bradshaw's Guide, Michael Portillo embarks on a journey through Britain's industrial heartland in the footsteps of King George V. He starts in Warrington and learns how the mayor, Dr George Joseph, received the royal party in the parlour of Warrington's magnificent town hall. Anthony Holland - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E5 ║ Birmingham to the Potteries ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: Michael Portillo reaches Birmingham and discovers how a radical reformer would make his mark on the city of a thousand trades. At Highbury Hall he finds Joseph Chamberlain's splendid mansion home and hears how he established a political dynasty including a Prime Minister and a Foreign Secretary. Anthony Holland - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Early 20th century Britain was reeling from industrial strife and suffragette outrages but the biggest crisis of all was the conflict in Ireland. Beginning in Newry, Michael finds a specially chartered train would deliver demonstrators campaigning for Irish Home Rule to a rally in the town. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: In Belfast's grand Edwardian City Hall, Michael investigates the scene of a watershed moment in Irish history and hears how thousands of Ulster Protestants were mobilised by train to sign a document pledging opposition to Home Rule for Ireland. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Leaving from the seaport of Larne Michael reaches Stranraerand the Mull of Galloway, where in a lighthouse built by railway engineer, Robert Stevenson, he discovers a magnificent machine, installed at the turn of the 20th century. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his journey through western Scotland by exploring the industrial heartland of Glasgow and its mighty River Clyde before taking the ferry to the island of Cumbrae. He is put to work behind the scenes at Glasgow's circular subway, explores the future of shipbuilding on the Clyde. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo falls into line with the University of Glasgow's Officer Training Corps. Founded in the early 20th century, the Corps flourishes today and Michael joins students for drill. From Glasgow, Michael heads west along the Firth of Clyde to Helensburgh, where he discovers a pioneering group of artists known as the Glasgow Boys. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E11 ║ Warwick to Radley ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: n Warwick's medieval castle he uncovers the scene of an extravagant and scandalous ball, which changed the life of its hostess, Daisy Greville, Countess of Warwick.At Cowley, Michael marvels at a spectacularly automated state-of-the-art production line producing 1,000 Minis a day and probes the pre-First World War origins of the Morris Oxford. Cassie Farrell - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E12 ║ Reading to Taplow ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: Michael Portillo picks up his rail journey from Warwick to Rye along the River Thames. In Reading, he traces the origins of education for workers. Messing about in boats is the name of the game in Henley on Thames, where Michael slips into a launch to hear about the world-famous regatta. Afternoon tea on the bank offers a chance to hear about four heroes of early 20th-century literary classic `The Wind in the Willows'. Cassie Farrell - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E13 ║ Ealing Broadway to South Kensington ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: Michael Portillo reaches the capital. In the Queen of the Suburbs, Ealing, he finds comedy at the home of British cinema and is transformed for the silver screen by expert hair and make-up. In Fulham, Michael heads underground to London's new super sewer, which is taking shape beneath the River Thames. In central London, he visits the London School of Economics and Political Science. Cassie Farrell - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Reno to Napa Valley ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Beginning in the Silver State of Nevada, Michael takes to the skies over the dramatic Sierra Nevada mountain range. At Lake Tahoe, he hears of the first European explorer, known as `The Pathfinder', whose discovery opened up the west for settlement. Travelling on the historic Virginia and Truckee heritage line, Michael investigates the vast deposits of silver and gold ore on which Virginia City was built. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.desc: Armed with his trusty Appleton's Guide, Michael Portillo reaches San Francisco, where he boards one of the city's iconic cable cars. Behind the scenes in the engineering powerhouse, he uncovers the street cars' secret to scaling the city's famously steep hills. In the Presidio neighbourhood, a leading publisher introduces Michael to San Francisco's long tradition of fine printing and book-making. Michael takes the opportunity to have his own treasured book appraised. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Berkeley to Santa Cruz ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Following his Appleton's guide, Michael Portillo makes a trip to the jewel in the crown of America's National Parks, Yosemite, to behold its towering granite cliffs, its giant sequoia trees and cascading waterfalls. He discovers how early conservationists fought to protect it in law and encounters a `buffalo soldier' in the heart of the forest. In Berkeley, Michael uncovers a catastrophic event, which hit the city of San Francisco hard in 1906. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Monterey to Los Angeles ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Steered by his late 19th-century Appleton's guidebook, Michael Portillo continues through southern California aboard the Coast Starlight rail service. In the historic port of Monterey, Michael raises the Bear Flag of the one-time Republic of California and above it, the Stars and Stripes. He discovers the city's Spanish and Mexican heritage and traces how the former fishing port described as `stinking and decrepit' in John Steinbeck's novel, `Cannery Row', has become a beacon for tourists. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Los Angeles to San Diego ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Michael Portillo strikes oil in the suburbs of Los Angeles, contemplates his navel in the orange groves of Riverside, makes a California roll and paints a pretty picture in Laguna Beach. It is Mexican Independence Day and the locals are celebrating the country's hard-won independence from Spain in the early 19th century. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: S3E2 ║ Boston to Concord ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Michael Portillo's nineteenth-century Appleton's guidebook leads him to the Parker House Hotel, where in his best pinny, he whisks up a Boston cream pie. In the fine dome atop Massachusetts General Hospital, where no-one could hear the screaming, Michael discovers the scene of grisly surgery, first made bearable, in 1846, by a miraculous new substance. North of Boston, in Salem, Michael is caught up in a witch hunt. Chris Bairstow - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Plymouth to New London ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Guided by his Appleton's and tracing the footsteps of the Pilgrim Fathers, Michael Portillo heads for Plymouth, the `home town' of America. He learns how indigenous tribes of Wamponoag people taught newly arrived settlers to live off the land, inspiring one of the biggest holidays in today's American calendar. Chris Bairstow - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: New Haven to Plattsburgh: Reversion ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Armed with his Appleton's guide, Michael Portillo continues his rail journey through Connecticut and New England. He takes a crash course in rowing in New Haven, where college teams from Yale and Harvard have battled for victory on the water since 1852. In Vermont, Michael visits a 19th-century farm, where the rich milk from prized Jersey cows imported from the British Isles supplied a thriving butter industry. Chris Bairstow - Director Cassie Farrell - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Montreal to Ottawa ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: In the vibrant metropolis of Montreal, Michael discovers how French and British colonial roots have influenced the city's construction, cuisine and culture. Undaunted by his guidebook's description of the treacherous Lachine Rapids, he gets a thorough soaking on a white-knuckle boat ride down the St Lawrence River. Cassie Farrell - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Thousand Islands to Toronto ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Steered by his 1899 Appleton's guide, Michael Portillo's rail journey through eastern Canada continues along the Grand Trunk railway, following the route of the St Lawrence River. At Brockville, he leaves the tracks for a nautical pilgrimage through the beautiful Thousand Islands. In the port city of Kingston, Ontario, Michael visits Fort Henry and, dressed for the occasion, is entrusted to fire the naval guns that protected the nation's southern border during the 19th century. Cassie Farrell - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S12E2 ║ Stoke Mandeville to Beaconsfield ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2021
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his travels through England's Home Counties at Stoke Mandeville in Buckinghamshire, where he discovers the legacy of a German Jewish doctor who fled the Nazis to settle in Britain. Tom Richardson - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Industrial Age
programme.sub-title: Wind, Water and Steam ║ Documentary / History ║ 1999
programme.desc: Beginning with a look at the early use of wind and water power, Fred traces the development of the steam engine and visits a man who has built a windmill in his own back garden. He then sets off in search of early beam engines that are still functioning today. David Hall - Director Fred Dibnah - Host.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Industrial Age
programme.desc: Travelling from the Scottish countryside of New Lanark to Burnley, Fred talks to ex-weavers about life in the mills and meets a group of volunteers who have spent 30 years saving mill engines. David Hall - Director Fred Dibnah - Host.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Industrial Age
programme.desc: Fred shifts his attention to the development of the iron and steel industries, starting with Ironbridge Gorge in Shropshire. He comes across a rolling mill which he remembers once operating in Bolton, tries his hand at chain making, and then it's eyes-on-stalks time as Fred drives the biggest steam rolling mill engine he has ever seen. David Hall - Director Fred Dibnah - Host.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Industrial Age
programme.desc: Starting in Cornwall and travelling all the way to Scotland, Fred turns his eye to the practice of mining. On his travels, he finds out exactly how tin, slate, lead and coal were all extracted from the ground. David Hall - Director Fred Dibnah - Host.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Industrial Age
programme.desc: Fred's fascinating journey through Britain's industrial past sees him tracing the development of the railways, from the first steam locomotive to the record-breaking Mallard. The excitement reminds him of his childhood days when locomotives used to roar past his bedroom window, and Fred gets his hands dirty stoking the boiler of a Black Five as he speeds through the Welsh countryside. David Hall - Director Fred Dibnah - Host.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Industrial Age
programme.desc: Fred moves on to the golden age of shipbuilding, examining the skills of engineers who turned Britain into one of the foremost manufacturing nations. He also visits the world's first production line in Suffolk. David Hall - Director Fred Dibnah - Host.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Age of Steam
programme.sub-title: The Early Pioneers ║ Documentary / History / Science ║ 2003
programme.desc: Fred visits Cornwall to look at the early history of the steam engine, first developed to pump water from tin mines. Fred Dibnah - Host.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Age of Steam
programme.sub-title: The Age of the Steam Locomotive ║ Documentary / History / Science ║ 2003
programme.desc: Fred Dibnah tells the story of the revolution in transport brought about by steam power, from the earliest colliery railways to the end of steam operation on Britain's rail network in the 1960s. Fred Dibnah - Host.

programme.title: James May's Man Lab
programme.desc: James May attempts to prove the impossible - that an Englishman can take a penalty and score. He will need to keep a cool head as he'll be taking the penalty in front of 20,000 baying German fans on the exact spot where England were knocked out of the 2006 World Cup. Plus, James reinstates an ancient ferry crossing, creates an indoor garden and builds the world's first multi-functional Swiss Army Bike. James May - Host.

programme.title: James May's Man Lab
programme.desc: In this Christmas special, James and the team try to create their own Christmas miracle, by making it snow. Oz Clarke is dispatched in a small plane armed with a salt shaker to see if cloud seeding really will produce the desired effect. Back in the `Man Lab', James invents a Christmas tree decorating blunderbuss gun and discovers the easiest way to wrap presents. James May - Host.

programme.title: James May's Man Lab
programme.desc: James May and the team set off chasing storms across the country as they attempt to take on the wrath of Mother Nature and actually catch a bolt of lightning. Also, James finally thinks he has found a sport he can compete in when he enters the Rock Paper Scissors World Championships. Further, there is an attempt to bring down Britain's crime figures by creating a neighbourhood watch team made up entirely of cats. James May - Host.

programme.title: James May's Man Lab
programme.desc: James May travels to an Oxfordshire town where a royal tradition desperately needs his help. Can he find a way of feeding thousands of locals to save their Diamond Jubilee celebration using ballistics and hot crossed buns? `Man Lab' also tests once and for all whether it is possible to make your own luck by beating the odds. James May - Host.

programme.title: Planet Earth II

programme.sub-title: S10E1 ║ Warrington to Preston ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: Armed with his early 20th century Bradshaw's Guide, Michael Portillo embarks on a journey through Britain's industrial heartland in the footsteps of King George V. He starts in Warrington and learns how the mayor, Dr George Joseph, received the royal party in the parlour of Warrington's magnificent town hall. Anthony Holland - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E5 ║ Birmingham to the Potteries ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: Michael Portillo reaches Birmingham and discovers how a radical reformer would make his mark on the city of a thousand trades. At Highbury Hall he finds Joseph Chamberlain's splendid mansion home and hears how he established a political dynasty including a Prime Minister and a Foreign Secretary. Anthony Holland - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Early 20th century Britain was reeling from industrial strife and suffragette outrages but the biggest crisis of all was the conflict in Ireland. Beginning in Newry, Michael finds a specially chartered train would deliver demonstrators campaigning for Irish Home Rule to a rally in the town. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: In Belfast's grand Edwardian City Hall, Michael investigates the scene of a watershed moment in Irish history and hears how thousands of Ulster Protestants were mobilised by train to sign a document pledging opposition to Home Rule for Ireland. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Leaving from the seaport of Larne Michael reaches Stranraerand the Mull of Galloway, where in a lighthouse built by railway engineer, Robert Stevenson, he discovers a magnificent machine, installed at the turn of the 20th century. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo continues his journey through western Scotland by exploring the industrial heartland of Glasgow and its mighty River Clyde before taking the ferry to the island of Cumbrae. He is put to work behind the scenes at Glasgow's circular subway, explores the future of shipbuilding on the Clyde. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo falls into line with the University of Glasgow's Officer Training Corps. Founded in the early 20th century, the Corps flourishes today and Michael joins students for drill. From Glasgow, Michael heads west along the Firth of Clyde to Helensburgh, where he discovers a pioneering group of artists known as the Glasgow Boys. George Boyle - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E11 ║ Warwick to Radley ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: n Warwick's medieval castle he uncovers the scene of an extravagant and scandalous ball, which changed the life of its hostess, Daisy Greville, Countess of Warwick.At Cowley, Michael marvels at a spectacularly automated state-of-the-art production line producing 1,000 Minis a day and probes the pre-First World War origins of the Morris Oxford. Cassie Farrell - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E12 ║ Reading to Taplow ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: Michael Portillo picks up his rail journey from Warwick to Rye along the River Thames. In Reading, he traces the origins of education for workers. Messing about in boats is the name of the game in Henley on Thames, where Michael slips into a launch to hear about the world-famous regatta. Afternoon tea on the bank offers a chance to hear about four heroes of early 20th-century literary classic `The Wind in the Willows'. Cassie Farrell - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: S10E13 ║ Ealing Broadway to South Kensington ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2019
programme.desc: Michael Portillo reaches the capital. In Fulham, Michael heads underground to London's new super sewer, which is taking shape beneath the River Thames. In central London, he visits the London School of Economics and Political Science. Cassie Farrell - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Reno to Napa Valley ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Beginning in the Silver State of Nevada, Michael takes to the skies over the dramatic Sierra Nevada mountain range. At Lake Tahoe, he hears of the first European explorer, known as `The Pathfinder', whose discovery opened up the west for settlement. Travelling on the historic Virginia and Truckee heritage line, Michael investigates the vast deposits of silver and gold ore on which Virginia City was built. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.desc: Armed with his trusty Appleton's Guide, Michael Portillo reaches San Francisco, where he boards one of the city's iconic cable cars. Behind the scenes in the engineering powerhouse, he uncovers the street cars' secret to scaling the city's famously steep hills. In the Presidio neighbourhood, a leading publisher introduces Michael to San Francisco's long tradition of fine printing and book-making. Michael takes the opportunity to have his own treasured book appraised. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Berkeley to Santa Cruz ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Following his Appleton's guide, Michael Portillo makes a trip to the jewel in the crown of America's National Parks, Yosemite, to behold its towering granite cliffs, its giant sequoia trees and cascading waterfalls. He discovers how early conservationists fought to protect it in law and encounters a `buffalo soldier' in the heart of the forest. In Berkeley, Michael uncovers a catastrophic event, which hit the city of San Francisco hard in 1906. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Monterey to Los Angeles ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Steered by his late 19th-century Appleton's guidebook, Michael Portillo continues through southern California aboard the Coast Starlight rail service. In the historic port of Monterey, Michael raises the Bear Flag of the one-time Republic of California and above it, the Stars and Stripes. He discovers the city's Spanish and Mexican heritage and traces how the former fishing port described as `stinking and decrepit' in John Steinbeck's novel, `Cannery Row', has become a beacon for tourists. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Los Angeles to San Diego ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Michael Portillo strikes oil in the suburbs of Los Angeles, contemplates his navel in the orange groves of Riverside, makes a California roll and paints a pretty picture in Laguna Beach. It is Mexican Independence Day and the locals are celebrating the country's hard-won independence from Spain in the early 19th century. Dave Minchin - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: S3E2 ║ Boston to Concord ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Michael Portillo's nineteenth-century Appleton's guidebook leads him to the Parker House Hotel, where in his best pinny, he whisks up a Boston cream pie. In the fine dome atop Massachusetts General Hospital, where no-one could hear the screaming, Michael discovers the scene of grisly surgery, first made bearable, in 1846, by a miraculous new substance. North of Boston, in Salem, Michael is caught up in a witch hunt. Chris Bairstow - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.title: Great American Railroad Journeys
programme.sub-title: Series 3 : Plymouth to New London ║ Documentary / Travel ║ 2018
programme.desc: Guided by his Appleton's and tracing the footsteps of the Pilgrim Fathers, Michael Portillo heads for Plymouth, the `home town' of America. He learns how indigenous tribes of Wamponoag people taught newly arrived settlers to live off the land, inspiring one of the biggest holidays in today's American calendar. Chris Bairstow - Director Michael Portillo - Host.

programme.desc: James May attempts to prove the impossible - that an Englishman can take a penalty and score. programme.title: James May's Man Lab
programme.desc: James May and the team set off chasing storms across the country as they attempt to take on the wrath of Mother Nature and actually catch a bolt of lightning. Further, there is an attempt to bring down Britain's crime figures by creating a neighbourhood watch team made up entirely of cats. James May - Host.

programme.title: James May's Man Lab
programme.desc: James May travels to an Oxfordshire town where a royal tradition desperately needs his help. Can he find a way of feeding thousands of locals to save their Diamond Jubilee celebration using ballistics and hot crossed buns? `Man Lab' also tests once and for all whether it is possible to make your own luck by beating the odds. James May - Host.
